Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: virtio_net: Denial of Service via use-after-free race condition
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

virtio_net: atomically disable rx mode work

virtio-net uses a boolean to gate rx_mode_work during device teardown.
The flag is changed under RTNL, but ndo_set_rx_mode checks it under the
address-list lock. A callback can therefore pass the check and enqueue work
after teardown has flushed it. The work is also enabled before late
probe operations that can fail, allowing probe unwind to free the netdev
with work still queued.

KASAN reports the worker using a virtqueue that probe unwind already freed:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in virtqueue_add_split
  Workqueue: events virtnet_rx_mode_work
  Call Trace:
   virtqueue_add_split (drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c:706)
   virtqueue_add_sgs (drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c:2839)
   virtnet_send_command_reply (drivers/net/virtio_net.c:3565)
   virtnet_rx_mode_work (drivers/net/virtio_net.c:3833)
   process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3322)
   worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3405)
  Freed by task 119:
   kfree (mm/slub.c:6625)
   vp_del_vq.isra.0 (drivers/virtio/virtio_pci_common.c:259)
   vp_del_vqs (drivers/virtio/virtio_pci_common.c:285)
   virtnet_probe (drivers/net/virtio_net.c:7129)

Use the workqueue disable mechanism to atomically reject new queue attempts
and drain running work. Keep work disabled until probe succeeds or restore
has reattached the netdev, then enable it and replay receive-mode state for
a running interface. Disable it before resource teardown in freeze and
remove.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via null pointer dereference in Speakup driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

speakup: Fix NULL pointer dereference on VT switch + selection

When selecting/pasting very quickly after VT switch, the tty is not set
yet, leading to a NULL dereference. We can just abort the operation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free in udlfb driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fbdev: udlfb: don't rebuild the mode list while the framebuffer is in use

dlfb_setup_modes() frees info->modelist with fb_destroy_modelist() and
rebuilds it, but fbcon holds raw pointers into that list in
fb_display[i].mode and nothing un-publishes them the way
do_unregister_framebuffer() and store_modes() do with
fbcon_delete_modelist(). The function does refuse to install a new mode
while the framebuffer has users (dlfb->fb_count != 0), but only after the
list is already destroyed. Reached from the 0666 "edid" sysfs attribute,
an unprivileged write to /sys/class/graphics/fb0/edid therefore fails with
-EINVAL and still leaves every fb_display[i].mode dangling; the next
console switch reads the freed fb_videomode in fb_videomode_to_var().

Test fb_count before touching the list. fbcon takes a reference through
fbcon_open(), so that condition covers exactly the states in which
fb_display[] points into the list, and the errno returned to userspace is
unchanged.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in fb_videomode_to_var (drivers/video/fbdev/core/modedb.c:905)
  Read of size 4 at addr ffff8880107b449c by task kworker/1:1/47
  Workqueue: events console_callback
  Call Trace:
   fb_videomode_to_var (drivers/video/fbdev/core/modedb.c:905)
   display_to_var (drivers/video/fbdev/core/fbcon.c:998)
   fbcon_switch (drivers/video/fbdev/core/fbcon.c:2182)
   redraw_screen (drivers/tty/vt/vt.c:994)
   complete_change_console (drivers/tty/vt/vt_ioctl.c:1141)
   console_callback (drivers/tty/vt/vt.c:3358)
   process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3396)
   worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3479 kernel/workqueue.c:3560)
   kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436)
   ret_from_fork (arch/x86/kernel/process.c:158)
   ret_from_fork_asm (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:245)
  ...
  The buggy address is located 28 bytes inside of
   freed 96-byte region [ffff8880107b4480, ffff8880107b44e0)

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: ceph: Denial of Service via crafted MDS map
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: reject mdsmaps that claim more than CEPH_MAX_MDS ranks

check_new_map() sizes its export-target bitmap from CEPH_MAX_MDS but walks
it with newmap->possible_max_rank, which comes straight off the wire:
ceph_mdsmap_decode() sets it to max(m_num_active_mds, m_max_mds), then
overwrites it with the size of the "in" set.  Neither is bounded by
CEPH_MAX_MDS, only by m_info allocating, so a monitor announcing more ranks
than the bitmap holds makes test_bit() read past the end of targets[].  The
clear_bit() loop above indexes the same bitmap, though it is additionally
bounded by mdsc->max_sessions.  The map arrives on the monitor connection,
which is unauthenticated in legacy msgr mode.

CEPH_MAX_MDS is a protocol constant from src/mds/mdstypes.h, and the
reserved inode ranges in super.h are laid out one rank apart over that
span, so a map claiming more ranks is corrupt.  Reject it where the rank
space is established rather than letting the count reach check_new_map().

  BUG: KASAN: stack-out-of-bounds in check_new_map (fs/ceph/mds_client.c:5968)
  Read of size 8 at addr ffffc90000ac7798 by task kworker/1:2/127
  Workqueue: ceph-msgr ceph_con_workfn
  Call Trace:
   <TASK>
   dump_stack_lvl (lib/dump_stack.c:94 lib/dump_stack.c:120)
   print_report (mm/kasan/report.c:378 mm/kasan/report.c:482)
   kasan_report (mm/kasan/report.c:595)
   kasan_check_range (mm/kasan/generic.c:186 mm/kasan/generic.c:200)
   check_new_map (fs/ceph/mds_client.c:5968)
   ceph_mdsc_handle_mdsmap (fs/ceph/mds_client.c:7060)
   extra_mon_dispatch (fs/ceph/super.c:802)
   mon_dispatch (net/ceph/mon_client.c:1483)
   ceph_con_process_message (net/ceph/messenger.c:1424)
   ceph_con_v1_try_read (net/ceph/messenger_v1.c:1430)
   ceph_con_workfn (net/ceph/messenger.c:1576)
   process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3396)
   worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3479 kernel/workqueue.c:3560)
   kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436)
   ret_from_fork (arch/x86/kernel/process.c:158)
   ret_from_fork_asm (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:245)
   </TASK>
  The buggy address belongs to stack of task kworker/1:2/127
   and is located at offset 288 in frame:
   check_new_map (fs/ceph/mds_client.c:5846)
  This frame has 1 object:
   [32, 288) 'targets'

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: ceph: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read during lease parsing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: require the dentry lease record to cover struct ceph_mds_reply_lease

parse_reply_info_lease() reads a 32-bit struct_len off the wire and only
checks that many bytes are present, without requiring struct_len to cover
sizeof(struct ceph_mds_reply_lease) (10 bytes).  A malicious MDS can
declare a shorter record and still get the pointer published: the
following *p += sizeof(**lease) overshoot is undone by *p = lend, so
nothing downstream rejects the reply.  ceph_fill_trace() ->
update_dentry_lease() then reads 10 bytes through that pointer on any
lookup on a mounted CephFS, running past the end of the message front.

Require the record to cover the structure, matching the sibling
parse_reply_info_dir().  A conforming MDS always encodes the full 10
bytes.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in __update_dentry_lease.constprop.0 (fs/ceph/inode.c:1459)
  Read of size 4 at addr ffff888026c63d65 by task kworker/0:3/2366
  Workqueue: ceph-msgr ceph_con_workfn
  Call Trace:
   __update_dentry_lease.constprop.0 (fs/ceph/inode.c:1459)
   ceph_fill_trace (fs/ceph/inode.c:1474 fs/ceph/inode.c:1823)
   mds_dispatch (fs/ceph/mds_client.c:4229 fs/ceph/mds_client.c:7225)
   ceph_con_process_message (net/ceph/messenger.c:1424)
   ceph_con_v1_try_read (net/ceph/messenger_v1.c:1430)
   ceph_con_workfn (net/ceph/messenger.c:1576)
   process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3396)
   worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3479 kernel/workqueue.c:3560)
   kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436)
   ret_from_fork (arch/x86/kernel/process.c:158)
   ret_from_fork_asm (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:245)

  The buggy address is located 357 bytes inside of
   allocated 360-byte region [ffff888026c63c00, ffff888026c63d68)

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: ksmbd: out-of-bounds read via DACL offset integer overflow
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check in build_sec_desc()

When the large dacl_offset is provided, dacl_offset + sizeof(struct
smb_acl) overflows on 32-bit builds and the check is passed,
Which makes le16_to_cpu(ppdacl_ptr->size) read out-of-bounds. This
only happens for dacl_offset in range [0xFFFFFFF8, 0xFFFFFFFF]. So
the oob read is max 8 bytes preceding the allocated ppntsd.

    unsigned int dacl_offset = le32_to_cpu(ppntsd->dacloffset);
    int ppdacl_size, ntacl_size = ppntsd_size - dacl_offset;

    if (!dacl_offset ||
	(dacl_offset + sizeof(struct smb_acl) > ppntsd_size))
	    goto out;

Commit beff0bc9d69b ("ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check")
fixes similar checks in other functions. But leaves this one out,
because it is only valid for 32-bit builds.

Reproduced on 32-bit ARM with KASAN, by a client sending SMB2
SET_INFO(SEC) with dacloffset=0xfffffff8, then QUERY_INFO(SEC) on the
same file:

 BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in build_sec_desc (fs/smb/server/smbacl.c:1105)
 Read of size 2 at addr c2a273fa by task kworker/1:1/35
 CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 35 Comm: kworker/1:1 Not tainted 7.3.0-rc2+ #5
 Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work
 Call trace:
  kasan_check_range from build_sec_desc (fs/smb/server/smbacl.c:1105)
  build_sec_desc from smb2_query_info (fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c:7676)
  smb2_query_info from handle_ksmbd_work (fs/smb/server/server.c:160)
  handle_ksmbd_work from process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3401)
  process_one_work from worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3473)
  worker_thread from kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436)

Add overflow check.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via corrupted UDF filesystem symlink
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

udf: fix return value for non-recorded-allocated extents in udf_map_block()

When someone creates a corrupted UDF filesystem where symlink contains
other extent type than EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED, it can leads to a crash
like:

 Oops: general protection fault
 KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access
 RIP: 0010:page_get_link (fs/namei.c:6503)
 Call Trace:
  vfs_readlink (fs/namei.c:6419)
  do_readlinkat (fs/stat.c:583)
  __x64_sys_readlink (fs/stat.c:605 fs/stat.c:602 fs/stat.c:602)

This is because in this case udf_map_block() fails to convert return
value of inode_bmap() from 1 to 0. Returned '1' propagates through
udf_bread() all the way up to __page_get_link() where it ends up being
treated as a folio pointer with obvious results.

Move the reset to 0 line outside the if, so udf_map_block() returns either
0 or -errno, even if the extent type is not EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: ksmbd: Denial of Service via invalid pointer dereference
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix invalid pointer dereference when get_inode_acl() fails

When get_inode_acl() fails, it returns an ERR_PTR(), but
ksmbd_acls_fattr() stored that pointer in smb_fattr without
checking for errors. Later callers then passed the error pointer
to security descriptor helpers or posix_acl_release(), resulting
in an invalid pointer dereference.

This was reproduced on an XFS-backed share when xfs_get_acl()
returned ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM). Querying the SMB ACL from a CIFS client
triggered the crash:

  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffffffffffffff8
  RIP: smb_acl_sec_desc_scratch_len+0x58/0x90 [ksmbd]
  Call Trace:
   smb2_query_info+0x40d/0x17c0 [ksmbd]
   handle_ksmbd_work+0x1ca/0x770 [ksmbd]

Fix this by checking the return values from get_inode_acl() in
ksmbd_acls_fattr(). Treat -EOPNOTSUPP as indicating that no ACL is
available, and propagate all other errors to the callers. Update
smb2_open() and smb2_get_info_sec() to handle these errors.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service via truncated HID reports in Roccat Kova[+] driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: roccat: kovaplus: reject short button reports

The raw event callback runs before HID core validates and zero-pads the
report.  It passes the buffer to helpers which inspect data[0] and read a
complete struct kovaplus_mouse_report_button for button reports.  A
truncated report can therefore cause an out-of-bounds read.

Require enough data for the button report before calling either helper.
Commit 47669bec44fe ("HID: asus: refactor the two workqueues and init
sequence") added the same kind of raw-event length validation to hid-asus.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via NULL pointer dereference in picoLCD driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: picoLCD: check for fb_deferred_io_init() error

fb_deferred_io_init() allocates deferred I/O state, populating
info->fbdefio_state, or leaving it NULL if an error occurs.

Currently picolcd_init_framebuffer() ignores its return value.

Therefore if an error arises in fb_deferred_io_init() (for instance, due
to an allocation failure) info->fbdefio_state is left NULL.

When the file is subsequently opened, fb_open() will dereference a NULL
pointer (calling fb_deferred_io_open()).

Fix this by checking for the error.

Also correct cleanup ordering - defio is initialised after the sysfs file,
so cleanup defio first.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in MCP2200 driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: mcp2200: validate READ_ALL response length

The HID core invokes raw_event callbacks before validating the report
length.  mcp2200_raw_event() casts a READ_ALL response to struct
mcp_read_all_resp and reads fields through offset ten without checking that
the response contains the structure.

A one-byte READ_ALL response reproduced the issue under KASAN:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in mcp2200_raw_event+0x24b/0x3a0
  Read of size 1 by task hidtrigger/89
  Call Trace:
   mcp2200_raw_event+0x24b/0x3a0
   kasan_report+0x139/0x170

Reject an incomplete READ_ALL response with a protocol error before reading
its fields.  The common completion path then wakes the command waiter with
the error instead of leaving it to time out.

Commit 47669bec44fe ("HID: asus: refactor the two workqueues and init
sequence") added the same kind of raw_event length validation to hid-asus.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via unvalidated report length in cp2112 driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: cp2112: validate response report lengths

The HID core invokes raw_event callbacks before validating the report
length.  cp2112_raw_event() reads every field of a transfer status response
without checking size.  For a data response, it reads the length at offset
two and copies that many bytes from offset three, again without ensuring
that the input report contains them.

Require a complete transfer status structure.  For data responses, first
require the header and then ensure the clamped payload length fits in the
received report before copying it.

Commit 47669bec44fe ("HID: asus: refactor the two workqueues and init
sequence") added the same kind of raw_event length validation to hid-asus.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via invalid bit shift in s32ton()
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: core: Fix out-of-bounds left shift by 32 in s32ton()

Syzbot reported an out-of-bounds shift (32-bit integer shifted left by
32) in the s32ton() routine in the HID core.  This routine converts a
signed 32-bit integer to a signed n-bit integer, and it caps the value
of n at 32.  But when n == 32 there's no need to do anything; it can
simply return the input value.  This will avoid calculating (1 << n)
when n is 32, which was the cause of the invalid shift.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: improper sensor report handling in AMD SFH driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: amd_sfh: Use report type from request node

Use report type from request node while sending feature and input reports
to HID core. The cli_data report type array is never assigned and
feature reports are sent as input reports.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via missing preemption disabling in KVM PowerPC Book3S
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: Add preempt_disable() around virtual-mode HPTE bit-lock users

kvmppc_hv_find_lock_hpte() requires virtual-mode callers to run with
preemption disabled, because it can return with HPTE_V_HVLOCK still held
until the caller later unlocks the HPTE.  Existing virtual-mode callers
in book3s_64_mmu_hv.c already follow that rule.

Two virtual-mode call paths do not:

1. kvmppc_handle_exit_hv() calls kvmppc_hpte_hv_fault() for hash-mode
   data-side and instruction-side faults after guest exit, with
   preemption already enabled.  kvmppc_hpte_hv_fault() calls
   kvmppc_hv_find_lock_hpte() directly.

2. kvmppc_pseries_do_hcall() executes virtual-mode handlers for HPT
   hcalls via kvmppc_pseries_do_hpt_hcall() with preemption enabled.
   The handlers for H_ENTER, H_REMOVE, H_READ, H_CLEAR_MOD, H_CLEAR_REF,
   H_PROTECT, and H_BULK_REMOVE spin on try_lock_hpte() or lock_rmap(),
   and H_ENTER also reaches kvmppc_do_h_enter(), which uses
   arch_spin_lock() on kvm->mmu_lock.  That raw lock choice is
   intentional because kvmppc_do_h_enter() is also used by real-mode
   callers, so the correct fix is to establish the proper preemption
   context at the virtual-mode caller boundary.

If a vCPU thread is preempted while holding HPTE_V_HVLOCK, any other
thread on the same CPU trying to acquire the same bit-lock can spin
indefinitely.  The same applies to lock_rmap() users and to the H_ENTER
path while holding the raw mmu_lock.

Fix this by adding preempt_disable()/preempt_enable() pairs around the
two kvmppc_hpte_hv_fault() call sites in kvmppc_handle_exit_hv(), and
around the kvmppc_pseries_do_hpt_hcall() invocation in
kvmppc_pseries_do_hcall().  Targeting only the HPT hcall helper avoids
wrapping non-HPT hcalls (such as H_RTAS, H_CONFER, H_REGISTER_VPA) that
perform page faults, blocking memory allocations, or context switches.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Use-after-free in KVM via race condition during memory invalidation
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Take SRCU in kvm_zap_gfn_range()

kvm_zap_gfn_range() walks memslots and rmaps and may drop mmu_lock to
reschedule. Callers that do not already hold kvm->srcu (or slots_lock)
can race with memslot deletion: synchronize_srcu_expedited() does not
wait, kvm_free_memslot() frees the old slot and its rmap, and the zap
resumes on freed memory.

The VFIO noncoherent-DMA path hits this by zapping the entire GPA
space without SRCU. KASAN reported:

  BUG: KASAN: vmalloc-out-of-bounds in slot_rmap_walk_next+0x82/0x1c0
  Read of size 8 at addr ffffc900005c1008
  Call Trace:
   slot_rmap_walk_next+0x82/0x1c0
   __kvm_rmap_zap_gfn_range+0x17a/0x280
   kvm_zap_gfn_range+0x2a6/0x6a0
   kvm_vfio_set_attr+0x576/0x770
   kvm_device_ioctl+0x1ff/0x3b0

Take SRCU inside kvm_zap_gfn_range() so every caller is covered.
Nesting with an existing kvm->srcu critical section is fine; the
helper uses a local index. Drop the now-redundant SRCU pair from
__kvm_set_or_clear_apicv_inhibit().

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: KVM: Denial of Service via missed nested exception VM-exits
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Request event processing for exception VM-Exits

Request event processing whenever kvm_queue_exception_vmexit() queues an
exception VM-Exit.  Most callers reach the helper through
kvm_multiple_exception(), which already sets KVM_REQ_EVENT, but nested
asynchronous page faults call it directly.

Without another event request, vcpu_enter_guest() skips
kvm_check_and_inject_events() and re-enters L2.  A subsequent VM-Exit can
clear the pending exception while reconstructing vectoring state, losing
the synthetic #PF VM-Exit.  The APF reason remains PAGE_NOT_PRESENT and a
later regular #PF can consume the stale value.

Setting KVM_REQ_EVENT in the common helper ensures that L1 receives the
queued VM-Exit before KVM re-enters L2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via unaligned Xen vcpu_info registration in KVM
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86/xen: Enforce 4-byte alignment of vcpu_info registration

Xen's map_guest_area() enforces that vcpu_info is aligned to
sizeof(xen_ulong_t). KVM has no such check, allowing a guest to
register vcpu_info at an arbitrary byte alignment.

Enforce unconditional 4-byte alignment regardless of the current
shinfo mode. This is sufficient because subsequent commits ensure
that all locked atomic operations on vcpu_info fields use at most
32-bit accesses. Return -ENXIO on failure, matching Xen's
map_guest_area() behaviour for unaligned requests.

Originally observed in review of an unrelated patch:
https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260604193554.1BA311F00893@smtp.kernel.org/

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds access in KVM MMU page walker
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86/mmu: Bug the VM if KVM attempts to walk more levels than the MMU has

Extend the "EFER.LMA && !CR4.PAE" check, which exists largely to guard
against KVM configuring a paging32 MMU with more than 2 levels of paging,
with a very explicit check for exactly that: that KVM isn't trying to walk
more levels of paging than the MMU template provides.  I.e. harden KVM
against all bugs that would cause KVM to generates accesses beyond the
bounds of guest_walker's arrays, regardless of how KVM ended up with the
misconfigured MMU.

Note, don't use w->cpu_role.base.level directly as the paging64 template
only provides two levels of page tables for PAE paging on 32-bit hosts, and
handles the third level by manually emulating the PDPTR access.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service via improper nested guest register handling in KVM
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: nSVM: Ignore EFER.LMA if EFER.LME=0 when preparing L2 state

Force EFER.LMA=0 if EFER.LME=0 when preparing L2 state for VMRUN, i.e.
mimic real hardware's behavior of ignoring EFER.LMA if EFER.LME=0.  VMRUN
unfortunately allows the nonsensical combination, i.e. doesn't fail, but
KVM itself has an invariant EFER.LMA can be set et if and only if EFER.LME
is set.   Breaking that invariant can lead to a variety of issue,
particularly in MMU code that keys off EFER.LMA when determining whether to
emulate/virtualization 4/5-level paging versus PAE paging.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free in SUNRPC transport tracing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

SUNRPC: trace an accepted transport before publishing it

svc_handle_xprt() publishes a newly accepted transport before tracing
it. svc_add_new_temp_xprt() places the transport on sv_tempsocks and
clears XPT_BUSY, so another nfsd thread can dequeue it at once. If the
peer has already closed the connection, that thread runs
svc_delete_xprt(), which drops the list reference, the only reference
the new transport holds. trace_svc_xprt_accept() then reads the
transport's addresses and network namespace from freed memory.

Before publication the accepting thread owns the transport
exclusively: XPT_BUSY is still set from svc_xprt_init() and the
transport is on no list. Emit the tracepoint there.

[ cel: trace before publication instead of taking an extra reference ]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service via kernel stack exhaustion in SUNRPC subsystem
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

SUNRPC: Reject a socket that already has an svc_sock attached

Writing the same socket descriptor to /proc/fs/nfsd/portlist twice
attaches a second svc_sock to one socket. svc_setup_socket() saves
the socket's callbacks before installing its own, so the second
attach records svc_write_space() as the old write_space callback.
svc_udp_init() invokes that callback by way of svc_sock_setbufsize(),
and svc_write_space() then calls itself until the kernel stack is
exhausted:

  BUG: TASK stack guard page was hit at ffffc900037d7ff8
   svc_write_space+0x90/0x2b0 net/sunrpc/svcsock.c:429
   svc_write_space+0xe6/0x2b0 net/sunrpc/svcsock.c:430
   ... 700 more ...
   svc_sock_setbufsize+0x18d/0x220 net/sunrpc/svcsock.c:386
   svc_udp_init net/sunrpc/svcsock.c:854 [inline]
   svc_setup_socket+0xb2f/0x1090 net/sunrpc/svcsock.c:1498
   svc_addsock+0x2fd/0x760 net/sunrpc/svcsock.c:1547
   __write_ports_addfd fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c:742 [inline]
   write_ports+0xa5b/0xcc0 fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c:861
   nfsctl_transaction_write+0x106/0x1a0 fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c:112

svc_data_ready() and svc_tcp_state_change() chain through their saved
callbacks the same way, so a TCP descriptor added twice recurses on
the next incoming segment instead. Reaching any of this takes a
writer on portlist, and the nfsd filesystem sets no FS_USERNS_MOUNT,
so the reproducer needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the initial user namespace.

Reject a socket that already carries sk_user_data. svc_setup_socket()
overwrites that field unconditionally, so a socket some other
consumer has claimed is one NFSD would corrupt whether or not the
callbacks recurse.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via unmapped memory execution during GSS module unload
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sunrpc: pin gss module across auth_domain RCU free

A gss auth_domain stores a raw pointer to svcauthops_gss in
dom->flavour, and its release queues svcauth_gss_domain_release_rcu()
via call_rcu(). Both live in auth_rpcgss.ko text, and nothing pins the
module while a domain referencing it is reachable. rmmod auth_rpcgss
can therefore unmap that text while an NFSD export still holds a
reference to the domain.

The export cache is one such holder. When the export is finally
released, the domain reference drops from module text:

    svc_export_put()
      auth_domain_put(exp->ex_client)
        auth_domain_release()
          dom->flavour->domain_release(dom)   /* into module text */
            svcauth_gss_domain_release()
              call_rcu(&dom->rcu_head,
                       svcauth_gss_domain_release_rcu)

Once auth_rpcgss is unloaded, the domain_release call lands in
unmapped memory. The rcu_barrier() in exit_rpcsec_gss() does not
help: it waits only for callbacks already queued, and this one is
not queued until the export goes away.

NFSD's NFSv4 objects import symbols from auth_rpcgss.ko, so only a
server built without CONFIG_NFSD_V4 can unload auth_rpcgss while
exports still name a gss domain.

Take a module reference in svcauth_gss_register_pseudoflavor() before
publishing the domain and drop it at the end of
svcauth_gss_domain_release_rcu(). The rcu_barrier() then holds the
module image until this callback has returned.

[ cel: rewrote description ]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: denial of service via improper handling of TLS control messages in SUNRPC
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

SUNRPC: Do not credit control-record octets to the RPC stream

svc_tcp_sock_recv_cmsg() receives up to two octets into a local
buffer, and returns that count for any record type other than
TLS_RECORD_TYPE_ALERT. Nothing reached the caller's buffer, but
svc_tcp_read_marker() adds the count to sk_tcplen and
svc_tcp_read_msg()'s caller adds it to sk_datalen. The RPC stream
advances over octets it never received. The fragment marker is
assembled from stale sk_marker octets. The message body comes from
pages nothing wrote.

A conforming client reaches this. RFC 8446 Section 4.6.3 lets either
peer send KeyUpdate once it has sent its Finished, and svcsock has no
rekey path. kTLS leaves the partially consumed record on ctx->rx_list,
so the body drains two octets per svc_tcp_recvfrom() call. Each pair
is credited the same way.

Return -EAGAIN for a record that is not an alert. That is what
svc_tcp_sock_process_cmsg()'s default arm returned before the receive
moved into a local buffer.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: information disclosure via uninitialized NFSv4 COMPOUND tag padding in nfsd
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: zero NFSv4 COMPOUND tag padding

nfs4svc_encode_compoundres() copies the tag bytes into reserved XDR space
and skips directly to the aligned end of the field. xdr_reserve_space()
rounds the reservation up but does not initialize the padding bytes.

A remote client can choose a tag length that is not a multiple of four,
causing one to three stale bytes from the response page to be returned in
the COMPOUND reply.

Use xdr_encode_opaque_fixed() to copy the tag and clear its XDR padding.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via race condition in NFSD client tracking pipe initialization
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: Set nn->cld_net before registering the cld pipe

rpc_mkpipe_dentry() instantiates the pipe's dentry before it returns,
so the cld pipe can be opened as soon as nfsd4_cld_register_net() has
run. __nfsd4_init_cld_pipe() does not store the new cld_net in
nn->cld_net until after that call. cld_pipe_downcall() reaches the
cld_net only through that pointer and takes cn_lock without checking
it, so a write() that lands in the window oopses.

Store nn->cld_net once @cn is fully initialized and before the pipe is
registered, and clear it again when registration fails.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via improper error handling in nfsd SETXATTR decoding
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: propagate SETXATTR value decode errors

nfsd4_decode_setxattr() stores the status returned while assembling a
non-empty attribute value, but then unconditionally returns nfs_ok. An
allocation failure can therefore leave a NULL value buffer paired with a
non-zero length and allow compound processing to continue.

Return the decoder status so that the operation stops on the original
error.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in NFSD RPC status dump
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: Fix out-of-bounds read in the rpc_status dump

nfsd_nl_rpc_status_get_dumpit() loads args->opcnt and
args->ops separately, then walks ops[] before rechecking
rq_status_counter. A COMPOUND that completes between the two loads
runs nfsd4_release_compoundargs(), which zeroes opcnt and points ops
back at the eight-entry inline array. A dump that already sampled an
opcnt of 200 clamps it to the sixteen slots in rq_opnum, then indexes
iops[0..15]. iops is the last member of struct nfsd4_compoundargs and
rq_argp is allocated at exactly that size, so the walk runs off the
end of the allocation. The trailing recheck discards the sampled data,
but the read has already happened. NFSD_CMD_RPC_STATUS_GET carries
no GENL_ADMIN_PERM, so an unprivileged local user can repeat the dump
against a busy server until it lands in the window.

Sample opcnt and ops into locals, then finish the counter recheck
before dereferencing ops. An unchanged counter means both came from the
same COMPOUND, where opcnt cannot exceed what ops holds.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via premature upcall completion in NFSD
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: Don't complete a cld upcall the daemon has not read

cld_pipe_downcall() matches a reply to its upcall on the xid alone.
A write that arrives before the daemon has read that upcall
completes __cld_pipe_upcall() while its struct rpc_pipe_msg is still
queued on the pipe. The waiter returns, its stack frame goes away,
and the pipe keeps a list_head that points into it. The next
rpc_queue_upcall() walks that pointer:

  BUG: KASAN: vmalloc-out-of-bounds in __list_add_valid_or_report
  Read of size 8 at addr ffffc90007027950 by task syz.0.96/13066
   __list_add_valid_or_report+0x6a/0x130
   rpc_queue_upcall
   cld_pipe_upcall
   nfsd4_cld_grace_start
   nfsd4_cld_tracking_init

The pipe is mode 0600 in rpc_pipefs, so the trigger is a broken or
hostile nfsdcld rather than an unprivileged task.

Record whether the daemon has consumed the whole message and
complete only when it has. cld_pipe_destroy_msg() runs on every path
by which the pipe releases a message, so it can maintain that flag
under cn_lock. nfsdcld sends its -EINPROGRESS downcalls only after
reading the upcall, so the new check does not break the GraceStart
record stream.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service in NFSD via unsupported delegation callback operations
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: Do not send CB_RECALL_ANY to NFSv4.0 clients

deleg_reaper() sends CB_RECALL_ANY to every ACTIVE client holding
delegations, but CB_RECALL_ANY is an NFSv4.1 operation. An NFSv4.0
client's callback service accepts only CB_GETATTR and CB_RECALL, so it
replies OP_ILLEGAL. The decoder maps the unexpected opnum to -EIO, and
nfsd4_cb_done() marks the client's callback channel down.

Nothing brings the channel back. nfsd4_run_cb_work() sets NFSD4_CB_UP
only for a minor version above zero, and the only nfsd4_probe_callback()
call site an NFSv4.0 client reaches is nfsd4_setclientid_confirm(). One
visit from the reaper therefore leaves the channel marked down until the
client re-establishes its clientid. RENEW then returns
NFS4ERR_CB_PATH_DOWN for as long as the client holds delegations.
nfsd4_cb_channel_good() stops returning true, so the client is granted
no further delegations.

Skip clients at minor version zero.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Data corruption via improper XDR buffer handling in NFSD
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: copy SETXATTR data from all XDR buffer segments

nfsd4_vbuf_from_vector() manually copies the head followed by whole
pages starting at offset zero. This assumes that all remaining data
starts at the beginning of the page array and that no data is stored
in the tail.

However, nfsd4_decode_setxattr() passes an xdr_buf returned by
xdr_stream_subsegment(). Such a sub-buffer can have a nonzero
page_base and can span its page and tail segments. Ignoring that
layout can copy the wrong bytes into the value passed to
vfs_setxattr().

Use read_bytes_from_xdr_buf(), which observes the complete xdr_buf
layout.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Information disclosure via uncleared padding in nfsd GETXATTR replies
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: clear XDR padding in GETXATTR replies

nfsd4_vbuf_to_stream() uses a raw memcpy() for the first fragment of an
attribute value. xdr_reserve_space() aligns the reservation but does not
initialize the extra bytes. If the complete value fits in that fragment,
the loop that clears padding for the final fragment is never entered.

A remote client reading an attribute whose length is not a multiple of
four can therefore receive one to three stale bytes from the response
page.

Encode the first fragment with xdr_encode_opaque_fixed(), matching the
final-fragment path and ensuring that any XDR padding is zeroed.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via unbounded listener list in NFSD
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: cap the number of listeners accepted in listener_set

nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() matches each requested listener against the
existing set. The nested loop that does this is O(N * M), where N is the
requested count and M is the existing count. The loop runs under sv_lock
with bottom halves disabled. A userland request with a very large listener
list can therefore spin in atomic context for a long time.

Reject a request that carries more than NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024)
entries. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), before the code
takes any lock. The limit is far above any realistic configuration.

This patch does not cap M. Only the message size bounded N; real sockets
bound M. A listener_set result set is the requested set, so that path also
holds M at the cap, but __write_ports_addxprt() adds two listeners per call
and removes none, so repeated calls can push M past it. The worst case
under sv_lock is therefore 1024 * M, plus 1024 nla_parse_nested() calls.
Both interfaces require CAP_NET_ADMIN.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via uncompleted upcall in pNFS block layout
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

pnfs/blocklayout: Complete a device upcall when the pipe is closed

Once blkmapd has read a whole upcall, rpc_pipe_read() unlinks the
message from every pipe list, so the purges in rpc_pipe_release()
and rpc_close_pipes() no longer reach it. bl_upcall_ops supplies no
.release_pipe callback, and bl_pipe_destroy_msg() returns without
completing the upcall because a downcall is expected to follow. A
daemon that exits between the read and the write therefore strands
its waiter: bl_resolve_deviceid() sleeps in wait_for_completion()
and never returns, and it holds nn->bl_mutex across that wait, so
every later device resolution in the net namespace blocks behind
it.

Add a .release_pipe that completes an upcall blkmapd has consumed
and left unanswered. Completing an upcall retires it, so a message
the framework has already purged is no longer in flight and is not
completed a second time here.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via oversized UNC mount path in SMB client
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix buffer overflow in SMB2_tcon()

In SMB2_tcon(), unc_path is allocated with a fixed buffer size of
MAX_SHARENAME_LENGTH * 2 bytes (672 bytes). However, the user-controlled
UNC path (tree) length is passed to cifs_strtoUTF16(), which assumes the
destination buffer is large enough and writes strlen(tree) + 1 UTF-16 code
units.

Commit 62a1a439e0fd ("cifs: clean up handling of unc= option") removed the
length check on UNC mount options, allowing mount paths to exceed
MAX_SHARENAME_LENGTH while retaining the fixed-size buffer allocation in
SMB2_tcon(). Consequently, an oversized UNC string causes cifs_strtoUTF16()
to write past the end of the heap object, resulting in a slab-out-of-bounds
write. Furthermore, if a tree exceeds MAX_TREE_SIZE characters, strscpy()
truncates it in cifs_tcon::tree_name, causing subsequent reconnects or
failovers to fail.

Fix this by first verifying that the length of tree does not exceed
MAX_TREE_SIZE, returning -EINVAL if it does. Then, dynamically allocate
unc_path based on the length of tree so that it safely accommodates all
UTF-16 code units for paths within MAX_TREE_SIZE.

[pc: remove unused MAX_SHARENAME_LENGTH]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via race condition in SMB client tree connection teardown
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: don't resurrect an exiting tcon from cached dir workers

cfids_laundromat_worker() bumps tcon->tc_count for every expired open
cfid and queues cached_dir_offload_close() without checking whether the
tcon is already being torn down.  Racing with the final cifs_put_tcon(),
the tcon comes back from zero and gets torn down twice:

  T1                                  T2
  cifs_put_tcon()
   --tc_count == 0, TID_EXITING
   tconInfoFree()
    free_cached_dirs()
     cancel_delayed_work_sync()       cfids_laundromat_worker()
                                       ++tc_count == 1
                                       queue_work(serverclose_wq)
    kfree(tcon->origin_fullpath)
    kfree(tcon)
                                      cached_dir_offload_close()
                                       close_cached_dir()  [UAF]
                                       cifs_put_tcon()
                                        tconInfoFree()     [double free]

cached_dir_lease_break() also bumps tc_count without tc_lock, racing with
the laundromat's locked update.

Take the tcon reference through a helper that refuses once the tcon is
TID_EXITING or its refcount has dropped to zero.  Queued put_work and
close_work then always hold a tcon reference, so tconInfoFree() can't
run before they finish and free_cached_dirs() doesn't need to flush any
workqueue.  If the laundromat can't get a reference, put the cfid back on
the dying list for free_cached_dirs() to free; its handle goes away with
the tree connection.

The lease break path finds the tcon on ses->tcon_list under
cifs_tcp_ses_lock, so it can't see TID_EXITING, but it now takes tc_lock.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service via improper extent tree cursor handling in XFS quota repair
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: fix correction of unwritten extents in quota file data fork

LOLLM noticed a couple of problems with the code that fixes unwritten
mappings in the quota file's data fork: first, we should zero the ondisk
contents as part of converting them to "unwritten" just in case we crash
shortly after the conversion.  Second, and more importantly, it noticed
that we fail to resynchronize the iext tree cursor after modifying the
iext tree.  If the tree shape changes, we could be in a world of hurt.
Third, we should force a quotacheck if we reset an ondisk dquot.  Fix
all issues.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: xfs: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds memory access during inode repair
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: don't overrun incore inode when cleaning attr forks

LOLLM noticed that xrep_dinode_check_afork doesn't check for a
di_forkoff value that is so large that the attr fork would begin after
the end of the inode space.  This causes afork_{ptr,size} to be
nonsense.  What we really ought to do here is zap the attr fork.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: heap out-of-bounds write in XFS during log recovery
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: bound inode fork length against the fork size during log recovery

xlog_recover_inode_commit_pass2() copies an inode log item's data/attr
fork region into the inode buffer using the on-log region length without
bounding it against the fork capacity, e.g.:

	len = item->ri_buf[2].iov_len;
	memcpy(XFS_DFORK_DPTR(dip), src, len);

The only guard is an ASSERT, which is a no-op on production kernels
(CONFIG_XFS_DEBUG off), and xfs_dinode_verify() runs only after the copy.
A crafted image with a dirty log can therefore drive a heap out-of-bounds
write at mount time. The XFS_ILOG_DBROOT sibling already passes
XFS_DFORK_DSIZE as a bound; the DDATA/DEXT and ADATA/AEXT memcpy paths
did not.

Bound each logged fork region against the destination fork size before
copying it, and reject the log item with -EFSCORRUPTED when it does not
fit. Because the recovered inode is only verified after the fork data has
been copied in, the checks are done up front, before any memcpy into the
on-disk inode.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service via out-of-bounds read in XFS
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: bound da-node entry count against the correct geometry

xfs_da3_node_verify() bounds the node entry count against the larger of
the directory and attribute geometries because, as a buffer verifier, it
cannot tell whether the block belongs to the directory or the attribute
tree. When the directory block size exceeds the fs block size (e.g.
mkfs.xfs -n size=64k -b size=4k), an attribute node buffer is a single fs
block that holds only m_attr_geo->node_ents entries, yet a crafted attr
node may claim a count up to m_dir_geo->node_ents and still pass the
verifier.

xfs_da3_node_lookup_int() then indexes btree[] up to that count during
its binary search -- an out-of-bounds read via getxattr/listxattr on a
mounted crafted image.

The buffer verifier is the wrong place to tighten this: it has no fork
context, and the transaction-less read path used by getxattr does not run
xfs_da3_node_set_type() either. xfs_da3_node_lookup_int(), on the other
hand, always runs on that path and holds args->geo, the geometry of the
fork actually being searched. Bound the entry count against
args->geo->node_ents there, before walking the entries.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Heap buffer overflow via crafted XFS filesystem image
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: reject remote xattr entries with an out-of-range value length

xfs_attr3_leaf_verify_entry() validates a remote attribute entry's name
but never bounds its on-disk value length (xfs_attr_leaf_name_remote.
valuelen, a __be32). A crafted leaf with valuelen = 0x80000000 passes
the verifier and the CRC.

That length is later assigned into the signed int args->rmtvaluelen
(xfs_attr3_leaf_getvalue), becoming negative, which slips past the signed
-ERANGE check in xfs_attr_copy_value(); a getxattr() with a small buffer
then memcpy()s a full remote block into the small kvalue buffer
(xfs_attr_rmtval_copyout) -- a heap out-of-bounds write with
attacker-controlled content, from an unprivileged getxattr(2) on a
mounted crafted image.

Reject remote entries whose value length exceeds XFS_XATTR_SIZE_MAX in
the leaf verifier, so the malicious block is rejected at read time.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: xfs: out-of-bounds write via crafted attribute length
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: reject out-of-range attribute value lengths in xfs_attr_copy_value

xfs_attr_copy_value() takes the value length as a signed int and, for a
remote xattr, is handed args->rmtvaluelen.  That field is filled from the
on-disk __be32 xfs_attr_leaf_name_remote.valuelen in
xfs_attr3_leaf_getvalue(), so a crafted length such as 0x80000000 is
stored into the signed rmtvaluelen as a negative number.

The "buffer too small" guard in xfs_attr_copy_value() is a signed
comparison:

	if (args->valuelen < valuelen)
		return -ERANGE;

A negative valuelen therefore compares as smaller than the caller's
buffer size, skips the -ERANGE path, and is then used as a copy length,
leading to an out-of-bounds copy of a full remote block into a small
getxattr(2) buffer on a mounted crafted image.

Reject a value length that is negative or larger than the maximum xattr
size before it is used, so a bogus on-disk length can no longer slip
through the value copier.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in XFS scrub
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: mark overfull dabtree node blocks as corrupt

LOLLM observes that we need to range-check the dabtree node record count
before using it to index an array.  Fix that.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: xfs: File system corruption via unhandled directory tree repair error
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: abort dirtree repair if the live update hook dies

LOLLM notices that if the live update hook for the directory tree repair
code hits an error, it will set dl->aborted and stops working.  If the
repair code ever sees that condition, it ought to bail out immediately
instead of continuing with obsolete data.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: File system corruption via improper error handling in XFS repair
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: fix lost errno returned from xfarray_foliosort

LOLLM noticed that we stop the sort early but don't actually pass along
the error code, which could enable repair code to continue running with
an unsorted array.  Fix that.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: File system corruption via invalid XFS summary counter repair
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: don't repair fs summary counters with garbage

LOLLM noticed that if we scan the filesystem and come up with totally
garbage numbers for the summary counters, we don't actually mark the
scan incomplete.  Because we don't do this, repair can install the
garbage values into the filesystem, making things worse.  Don't do that.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: File system corruption via failed live updates during XFS directory repair
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: don't fix the directory tree if live update fails

LOLLM complains that we don't double-check dl->aborted one last time to
before committing repairs to the filesystem.  This is important because
the live update handler could have set ->aborted if it encountered a
runtime error.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via incorrect attribute fork reset in XFS
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: always reset incore attr fork buffer when resetting fork

LOLLM noticed that the local format attr fork verifier depends on
if_bytes being set correctly.  However, the fork reset function doesn't
reset that correctly, which can cause post-repair verifier failures.
Fix that.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: xfs: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds write in xfs_ioc_attr_list
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: fix buffer overruns in xfs_ioc_attr_list

When we converted the al_offset array in struct xfs_attrlist into a VLA,
the size of the object shrank by 4 bytes.  Unfortunately, the buffer
size validation in the attrlist ioctl wasn't updated to notice this, so
the al_offset[0] assignment blindly writes off the end of the buffer.
LOLLM noticed the omitted check and complained.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Data loss in OverlayFS via file handle operations on NFS-exported mounts
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: read the nlink xattr of every indexed non-dir

With nfs_export=on, data written through a file handle to a lower file,
i.e. a file that exists only in a lower layer of the overlay, can be
lost on the next mount. A lookup of the file by name then returns -EIO.
Also, a file with one name reports st_nlink 2 once it has been copied to
the upper layer. After such a file is removed, its file handle can still
open it until the next mount.

Before a lower file is changed for the first time, overlayfs copies it
to the writable upper layer. This is called copy up.

The index directory is $workdir/index, where $workdir is the directory
given by the workdir= option. Each entry is named after the file handle
of a lower inode, so that overlayfs can get from the handle to the
copied up inode.

With nfs_export=on, copy up indexes every non-directory: it copies the
file to an entry in the index directory and then hard links that entry
into the upper directory. The index entry is an extra link to the upper
inode, so overlayfs stores the link count that users should see in the
overlay.nlink xattr.

A file can also be opened by handle, either by an NFS client or by a
process with CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH calling open_by_handle_at(). If the
file is not in the dcache, its overlay dentry is disconnected, i.e. it
has no parent yet. Copy up then creates the index entry but no hard link
in the upper directory. The index entry has i_nlink 1 and holds the only
copy of the data written to the file.

ovl_get_nlink() reads the stored count. Its caller passes a default,
which the function returns if there is no stored count. If the lower
inode has i_nlink 1, the function returns the default without reading
the xattr. That was correct as long as only lower files with multiple
links were indexed.

On the next mount, ovl_verify_index() looks for orphans, i.e. index
entries of files whose last name was removed. For an index entry with
i_nlink 1, it passes a default of 0 to ovl_get_nlink() and treats a
result of 0 as an orphan. Here the lower inode also has i_nlink 1, so
the result is the default. ovl_indexdir_cleanup() then replaces the
entry with a whiteout, which in the index marks a file as deleted. The
written data is lost.

A lookup by name then returns -EIO, because a whiteout as the index
entry of a lower file that still exists is a bad index.

ovl_get_inode() gets the wrong count the same way. Its default is the
i_nlink of the upper inode, which includes the index entry, so a copied
up file with one name reports st_nlink 2.

When that name is removed, the count drops to 1 rather than 0.
ovl_nlink_end() replaces the index entry with a whiteout only at a count
of 0, so the entry stays, and the handle of the removed file still opens
it.

Reproduced by writing through open_by_handle_at() to an uncached lower
file with one link. After a remount the data was lost, and the name
returned EIO.

Fix this by adding an argument to ovl_get_nlink() that says whether the
caller found an index entry, and by skipping the xattr only if the
caller found none.

Known gaps:
- An index entry that a kernel without this patch left behind for a
  removed file now stays, and the handle of that file keeps working. The
  entry has i_nlink 1 and a stored count of 1, just like the entry of a
  file that was only written by handle. Without this patch, the next
  mount treated it as an orphan.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Information disclosure in OverlayFS via race condition during hard link creation
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: fix a torn path in ovl_get_redirect()

A hard link of a metacopy file that races with a rename of an ancestor
stores a redirect to the wrong lower file.

Each component of an absolute redirect must be the name that a dentry
has in the parent that the walk continues with. ovl_get_redirect()
copies the name under d_lock and calls dget_parent() after the unlock,
and the callers for a hard link hold no lock that stops a rename across
directories. A rename between the two steps combines the old name with
the new parent.

With delays in ovl_get_redirect(), an unprivileged user hard-linked a
metacopy file while renaming its ancestor to another directory, the
stored redirect named another lower path, and after a remount the file
showed the data of a root-only file.

Fix this by taking the parent first and checking it again under d_lock.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via missing directory validation in OverlayFS volatile mount
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: check that the parents of volatile/dirty are dirs

An unprivileged user crashes the kernel by mounting overlayfs with the
volatile option.

A dentry that serves as the parent of a lookup must be a directory.
ovl_create_volatile_dirty() walks work/incompat/volatile/dirty by name,
and ovl_lookup_or_create() returns an existing entry whatever its type.
A file or a symlink that another task creates during the mount becomes
the parent of the next lookup, which calls a NULL ->lookup.

An unprivileged user mounted overlayfs with "volatile" in a user
namespace while a second process created a symlink named work/incompat,
and the mount task oopsed on a NULL ->lookup call.

Fix this by returning -ENOTDIR from ovl_lookup_or_create() when the
caller asked for a directory and the existing entry is a non-dir.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: overlayfs: Denial of Service via NULL pointer dereference during directory copy-up
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: always encode the origin fh when index is enabled

On an overlay with index=on,nfs_export=on, copy up of a directory
crashes the kernel once an LSM has started to deny CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH
to the mounter, the task that mounted the overlay. The mount and the LSM
policy change require root. After that, any user who can write to a
directory that exists only in a lower layer triggers the oops by doing
so.

Before a file or directory that exists only in a lower layer is changed
for the first time, overlayfs copies it to the writable upper layer.
This is called copy up.

On copy up, ovl_get_origin_fh() encodes the file handle of the lower
inode, called the origin. It returns NULL if ovl_can_decode_fh() says
that the lower filesystem cannot decode handles. Whether the callers can
handle NULL depends on the index option:

- Without an index, NULL is fine: the callers store an empty origin
  xattr.
- With index enabled, overlayfs keeps entries for copied up inodes in an
  internal index directory. The name of an index entry is derived from
  the handle, so ovl_get_origin_fh() must return a handle or an error.

The mount only enables the index if ovl_can_decode_fh() succeeds for all
layers, but the result can change later. The function checks the export
operations of the filesystem and capable(CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH). Copy up
runs with the mounter's credentials, and an LSM can start to deny the
capability to those credentials after the mount. ovl_get_origin_fh()
then returns NULL with index enabled.

This goes wrong in two callers:

- With nfs_export=on, copy up of a directory creates an index entry for
  the directory. ovl_create_index() passes the NULL handle to
  ovl_get_index_name_fh(), which dereferences it.
- If the result changes while mount(2) is still running,
  ovl_get_indexdir() passes a NULL from ovl_get_origin_fh() to
  ovl_verify_set_fh() in the same way.

Before the commit in the Fixes tag, these two callers encoded the handle
themselves, without consulting ovl_can_decode_fh().

Reproduced with a BPF LSM program that started to deny the capability
after the mount. An unprivileged touch in a directory that had not been
copied up yet oopsed in ovl_get_index_name_fh(). With this patch the
touch succeeds and the directory gets its index entry.

Fix this by calling ovl_can_decode_fh() in ovl_get_origin_fh() only when
index is disabled.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free in OverlayFS
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: use the pinned upper dir in ovl_fix_origin()

Renames made directly on the upper filesystem during a lookup crash the
kernel.

A dentry that is passed to vfs_setxattr() must be pinned.
ovl_fix_origin() passes upper->d_parent to ovl_set_impure() without a
reference, and the lookup holds no lock of the upper directory. A
rename on the upper filesystem changes d_parent, and only the child
pins the new parent, so a second rename and an rmdir free it.

With delays in ovl_fix_origin() and ovl_set_impure(), renaming the upper
directory twice and removing the intermediate parent during the lookup
of a merge directory without an origin xattr gave a KASAN
use-after-free in vfs_setxattr().

Fix this by passing the upper dentry that the overlay parent holds.

[amir: add helper ovl_set_impure_dir()]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free in OverlayFS copy-up
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: take a snapshot of the name for copy up

The copy up of a directory reads a freed dentry name when a lookup
moves the directory at the same time.

A pointer to the name of a dentry is only valid while something stops
a move of the dentry. ovl_do_copy_up() keeps a plain copy of
c->dentry->d_name in c->destname, and ovl_copy_up_start() only keeps
ovl_rename() away. When a lookup finds the same directory under another
name after a change to the lower layer, d_splice_alias() moves the
dentry and frees its external name.

With a delay in ovl_do_copy_up(), a chmod of a lower-only directory with
a 60 byte name raced with a rename of that directory in the lower layer
and a stat of the new name, and KASAN reported a use-after-free in
lookup_noperm_common().

Fix this by using take_dentry_name_snapshot() for c->destname.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free in OverlayFS directory listing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: hold a reference on the parent in readdir

Listing a directory on an overlay uses a freed dentry and crashes the
kernel when a lookup moves the directory at the same time.

Code that can sleep may only use d_parent without a reference while
something stops a move of the dentry. ovl_iterate_real(),
ovl_need_adjust_d_ino() and ovl_cache_update() use the d_parent of the
listed directory and hold only the lock of that directory. When a
lookup finds the directory under another parent after a change to a
layer, d_splice_alias() moves it without that lock and drops its
reference on the old parent.

With a delay in ovl_iterate_real(), getdents64 on an overlay directory
raced a rename in the lower layer and a lookup that moved its dentry,
and after an rmdir of the old parent KASAN reported a use-after-free in
security_inode_getattr().

Fix this by using dget_parent() in the three functions.

[amir: fix comments in ovl_need_adjust_d_ino()]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Information disclosure via out-of-bounds memory read in SMB client
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix OOB last_entry pointer from unbounded LastNameOffset

CIFSFindFirst() and CIFSFindNext() locate the last entry of a
TRANS2_FIND_FIRST2 or TRANS2_FIND_NEXT2 response by adding the
LastNameOffset of the response parameters to the start of the data
area, and store the result in psrch_inf->last_entry. MS-CIFS 2.2.6.2.2
defines that offset as the offset of the entry's file name; the client
follows the reading of NT and Samba servers, which point it at the
entry. LastNameOffset is only checked against CIFSMaxBufSize, which
says nothing about the response actually received: validate_t2() lets
the data area start up to 1024 bytes into the buffer, and SendReceive()
copies at most CIFSMaxBufSize + MAX_CIFS_HDR_SIZE bytes of a response,
16468 by default, into a cifs_request allocation of CIFSMaxBufSize +
MAX_SMB2_HDR_SIZE bytes, 16588 by default. The pointer itself can
therefore be placed anywhere from the end of the received data to 820
bytes past the end of the allocation.

The read through that pointer is far larger than its displacement.
find_cifs_entry() hands last_entry to cifs_save_resume_key() after every
FindNext and after the FindFirst of a search rewind, and
cifs_fill_dirent() takes the length of the name from the entry itself: a
__le32 FileNameLength for most levels, a __u8 for
SMB_FIND_FILE_INFO_STANDARD, and for SMB_FIND_FILE_UNIX the result of a
scan for the terminating NUL over up to PATH_MAX + 1 UTF-16 units. The
name is recorded as the resume name of the search, and the next
CIFSFindNext() rejects only a recorded length of PATH_MAX or more before
copying the name into the ResumeFileName of its request and sending it
with the resume key taken from the same entry: up to 4 KiB of memory
from past the end of the allocation leaks to the server, and for
SMB_FIND_FILE_UNIX the NUL scan runs about twice as far before the
length is even known. The entry does not have to lie outside the
response for that either: a maximal response ends about 120 bytes before
the end of the allocation, so an entry in its last bytes with a name
just under PATH_MAX has nearly all of that name copied from past the
allocation.

It needs nothing unusual from the client: a FindNext response that
reports no entries and does not end the search makes find_cifs_entry()
send the next FindNext at once, carrying whatever was parsed at
LastNameOffset, and a search rewind can do the same after its
FindFirst. SMB1 is not negotiated by default: this takes a malicious
or compromised server, a mount of it with an explicit vers=1.0, which
CONFIG_CIFS_ALLOW_INSECURE_LEGACY (default y) permits, and a directory
listing on that mount.

With KASAN enabled, a response that places the last entry past the
buffer, with a large DataOffset and a LastNameOffset near the end of
its range, gives:

 ==================================================================
 BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in cifs_save_resume_key.isra.0+0x7aa/0x7f0
 Read of size 4 at addr ffff88807b55c33b by task ls/83

  <TASK>
  kasan_report+0xdf/0x1a0
  cifs_save_resume_key.isra.0+0x7aa/0x7f0
  cifs_readdir+0x1ed6/0x29c0
  iterate_dir+0x1c0/0x570
  __x64_sys_getdents64+0x133/0x270
  do_syscall_64+0x109/0x5d0
  entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
  </TASK>

 Allocated by task 83 on cpu 0 at 19.317556s:
  cifs_buf_get+0x36/0x90
  smb_init+0x4f/0x110
  CIFSFindNext+0xf7/0x14c0
  cifs_readdir+0xf51/0x29c0

 The buggy address belongs to the object at ffff88807b558000
  which belongs to the cache cifs_request of size 16588
 The buggy address is located 623 bytes to the right of
  allocated 16588-byte region [ffff88807b558000, ffff88807b55c0cc)

The four bytes read there are the FileNameLength of the entry, which
cifs_fill_dirent() tak

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free in OCFS2 trace events
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: snapshot dentry names in file and setattr traces

Patch series "ocfs2: stabilize dentry names in file and setattr traces",
v4.

Snapshot names at all six users of ocfs2__file_ops and at the separate
setattr event. Patch 1 handles the five ordinary file-operation callers
and setattr. Patch 2 handles release separately to preserve its locked
open-count sample and take the snapshot outside that critical section.

The release explanation distinguishes its existing RCU lifetime coverage
from name/length consistency. It does not claim that the ordinary
callers' external-name UAF interleaving crosses the held inode spinlock.
The release source change is unchanged from v3.

Patch 1 also removes the read callback's redundant NULL-inode check.
The two patches apply independently and leave trace formats unchanged.


This patch (of 2):

The open, fsync, read, write and splice-read trace calls pass the live
dentry name and length to the shared ocfs2__file_ops event class.
ocfs2_setattr() passes the same unprotected arguments to its own event.
Both events size and copy a __string field separately. A reference to
the dentry does not pin the external storage backing an individual name.

With an event enabled, a caller can be preempted after loading the name
pointer. A long-to-short rename can then replace the name and reclaim its
old external allocation before the trace callback sizes or copies it,
provided no other snapshot retains that allocation.

The setattr inode lock does not exclude every rename: a same-directory
rename of a source directory need not take that directory's inode lock.
It can therefore change the dentry name while setattr records its event.
Inline names and separately loaded lengths can also change during trace
record sizing and copying.

Take a dentry name snapshot around each of these six trace calls and
pass both the string and length from the snapshot. Check event enablement
before taking a snapshot. Keep the event classes and formats unchanged.

Also remove the redundant NULL-inode check in the read callback.
file_inode() returns the open file's inode, which is already used by the
trace call above the check.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service via use-after-free race condition in ocfs2
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: pin refcount trees before dropping the lookup lock

A refcount tree returned to ocfs2_lock_refcount_tree() must stay alive
until that caller releases its operation reference. However,
ocfs2_get_refcount_tree() returns the cached pointer after dropping
osb_lock, and the caller only takes its kref afterwards. The registry
reference does not protect this gap from concurrent removal.

This can happen when another node frees a refcount root and reuses its
block with a different generation while this mount retains the old
cached tree. Two local operations on different inodes sharing the new
root, such as data CoW and an external xattr update, can then look up
the same stale tree. Their inode locks are independent, and both the
REFCOUNT DLM lock and rf_sem are acquired after the first operation
reference.

The following ordering is possible, with no other operation references:

  Data CoW                         Xattr update
  --------                         ------------
  Look up the old tree under
    osb_lock, then drop osb_lock
                                   Look up the same tree and take a kref
                                   Acquire the tree locks and read the
                                     new on-disk generation
                                   Erase the old tree under osb_lock
                                   Unlock and drop the operation kref
                                   Drop the registry kref, freeing tree
  Take a kref through the
    freed tree pointer

The final kref_get() accesses freed rf_getcnt storage, and subsequent
accesses in ocfs2_lock_refcount_tree() also use the freed allocation.

Take the operation reference in ocfs2_get_refcount_tree() before
releasing osb_lock, including when an insertion loses to another lookup.
Removal must acquire the same lock, so it cannot drop the registry
reference before the lookup has pinned the tree. Keep the existing
unlock and error path puts. The two callers that already hold the
refcount tree lock keep their borrowed lookup behavior and do not
acquire an extra reference.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via crafted OCFS2 image mount
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: fix chunk number of the first chunk in a local quota file

Mounting a crafted OCFS2 image can corrupt kernel memory.  When the
local quota file header of such an image claims zero chunks, the first
quota entry allocated during the mount gets a chunk number taken from a
kernel pointer, and releasing that entry clears a bit far outside the
chunk bitmap.

The write will corrupt the data stored at that address, and the
corruption may lead to a system crash or damage unrelated data. 
Mounting requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN, so it takes an untrusted image, such
as removable media or a loop mount of a file from elsewhere.

Since the chunk number comes from a kernel pointer, the address of the
bit that gets cleared differs from boot to boot, and the issue has been
reported under several titles:

- BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KASAN: use-after-free Write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds Write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KASAN: slab-use-after-free Write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot
- KFENCE: use-after-free write in ocfs2_local_release_dquot

Note that none of these is a use-after-free in the quota code: the
chunk and its buffer head are alive.  The bit that gets cleared lies
far outside the bitmap.  KASAN and KFENCE name each report based on the
object occupying that address, which explains why the same issue is
reported under so many different titles.  In the report I sent, the
address fell in a free page, which KASAN labels use-after-free.

There are known reproducers.  Both a syzkaller and a C reproducer are
available from the Google Drive link [1] in my report thread.  The
issue was found by our modified syzkaller, not a theoretical thing
found by an LLM.  I have not seen it outside fuzzing, so it is not
affecting me in the real world.

The local quota file in OCFS2 is divided into chunks, and each chunk
begins with a header block holding a bitmap of the quota entries that
chunk has handed out.  Chunks are numbered from zero, and that number is
used to convert the file offset of an entry back into a bit position in
the bitmap.  ocfs2_local_quota_add_chunk() appends a new chunk to the
in-memory list and numbers it one past the chunk that was last:

	list_add_tail(&chunk->qc_chunk, &oinfo->dqi_chunk);
	chunk->qc_num = list_entry(chunk->qc_chunk.prev,
				   struct ocfs2_quota_chunk,
				   qc_chunk)->qc_num + 1;

The predecessor is looked up after the new chunk is added to the list, so
if the list was empty, the prev pointer is the list head itself.  The head
is the dqi_chunk member of struct ocfs2_mem_dqinfo and is not a chunk, so
reading qc_num through it lands 16 bytes past the start of the head, on
the dqi_gqinode pointer that follows it.  The first chunk of the file is
then numbered with the lower half of a kernel pointer instead of 0.

The list is empty when the local quota file header claims the file has no
chunks.  ocfs2_local_read_info() takes dqi_chunks from that header without
validating it, so an image with dqi_chunks == 0 takes this path when the
first quota entry is allocated.

ocfs2_create_local_dquot() turns the bad number into a file offset with
ol_dqblk_off(), which shifts a 32-bit block number left by the block size
bits, so the top bits of such a large block number are lost. 
ocfs2_local_release_dquot() turns the offset back into a bit index with
ol_dqblk_chunk_off(), using the full chunk number, so the lost bits push
that index far outside the bitmap, and clearing it corrupts unrelated
memory.

Compute the chunk number before putting the chunk on the list, and use 0
when the list is empty.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: ocfs2: Denial of Service via use-after-free during file system remount
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: cancel quota sync work before freeing quota info

OCFS2 quota info owns dqi_sync_work and must outlive both its timer and
qsync_work_fn().  ocfs2_local_free_info() frees that owner without
cancelling the work, relying on the quota suspend/disable wrappers.

Loading quotas on a read-only to read-write remount can successfully queue
the work in ocfs2_global_read_info() and then fail while attaching a dquot
to an existing inode in add_dquot_ref().  The quota core unwinds that
failure directly through dquot_disable(), bypassing the OCFS2 wrapper:

  Remount task (s_umount write)        Timer/workqueue
  ocfs2_global_read_info()
    schedules dqi_sync_work
  add_dquot_ref() returns an error
  dquot_disable()
    ocfs2_local_free_info()
      frees oinfo
                                     delayed-work timer expires
                                     qsync_work_fn() reads oinfo

The timer core can then write to the freed embedded timer, or
qsync_work_fn() can read oinfo->dqi_gqinode before its s_umount trylock.
The outer ocfs2_disable_quotas() cleanup skips the failed type because
dquot_disable() has already cleared its loaded state.

Cancel dqi_sync_work synchronously at the start of
ocfs2_local_free_info(), before dropping the global inode or freeing any
owner state. The work is initialized whenever read_file_info() succeeds.
dquot_disable() holds s_umount for write, so the callback skips its quota
scan via down_read_trylock() and can finish without waiting for teardown.
The synchronous cancel also handles its self-rearm.
