Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service (DoS) via oversized packets in Pegasus USB Ethernet driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: usb: pegasus: do not advance rx_skb->data on dropped frames

For the 0x8513 chip, read_bulk_callback() skips the 2-byte receive
header by advancing pegasus->rx_skb->data in place. This is done before
the pkt_len > PEGASUS_MTU check, and when that check drops the frame
the good path resubmits the same skb with the advanced rx_skb->data as
the transfer buffer, still PEGASUS_MTU bytes long.

Every frame with an oversized length field therefore moves the receive
buffer two more bytes towards the end of the skb data area. A device
that keeps sending such frames makes the host controller write received
data over skb_shared_info and past the end of the allocation, and the
corrupted skb_shared_info is used when the skb is eventually freed.
With an emulated device sending frames filled with 0x5a on a KASAN
kernel:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in dummy_timer+0xade/0x3f00 [dummy_hcd]
  Write of size 1536 at addr ffff888105821202 by task swapper/1/0
  ...
  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xeb4b474b4b4b4b4c: 0000 [#1] PREEMPT SMP KASAN NOPTI
  KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access in range [0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a60-0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a67]
  RIP: 0010:skb_release_data+0x36f/0x800

Only skip the header with skb_reserve() once the frame is going to be
passed up, so the receive buffer always starts at the beginning of the
skb data area. Unlike the old pointer adjustment, skb_reserve() also
moves skb->tail, so the two header bytes now count against the buffer
size: lower the length limit for the 0x8513 accordingly, otherwise a
pkt_len of PEGASUS_MTU - 1 or PEGASUS_MTU would trip skb_over_panic().

Found by code review with LLM assistance and reproduced with an
emulated USB device (raw-gadget + dummy_hcd).

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: usbtv: Denial of service via race condition on device disconnect
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: usbtv: fix null-pointer dereference on disconnect

A null-pointer dereference can occur in usb_make_path() when called from
usbtv_querycap() (and other ioctl handlers) during device disconnection.

Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
0xdffffc000000000a: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000050-0x0000000000000057]
RIP: 0010:usb_make_path include/linux/usb.h:985 [inline]
RIP: 0010:usbtv_querycap+0x9c/0x100
drivers/media/usb/usbtv/usbtv-video.c:612
...
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 v4l_querycap+0x236/0x470 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c:1106
 __video_do_ioctl+0x8af/0xc70 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c:3133
 video_usercopy+0x860/0x1430 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c:3475
 v4l2_ioctl+0x18d/0x1e0 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-dev.c:366
 vfs_ioctl fs/ioctl.c:51 [inline]
 __do_sys_ioctl fs/ioctl.c:597 [inline]
 __se_sys_ioctl+0xfc/0x170 fs/ioctl.c:583
 do_syscall_x64 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:63 [inline]
 do_syscall_64+0x174/0x580 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:94

This happens due to a race condition between the USB device disconnect
routine (usbtv_disconnect()) and V4L2 ioctls. When the device is
disconnected, usbtv_disconnect() sets usbtv->udev = NULL without holding
the usbtv->v4l2_lock mutex. Concurrently, an ioctl handler like
usbtv_querycap() can be executing under the v4l2_lock and attempt to use
usbtv->udev, leading to a crash.

To fix this, move the usbtv->udev = NULL assignment into usbtv_video_free()
and protect it with mutex_lock(&usbtv->v4l2_lock). This ensures that no
non-queue ioctl handler can run concurrently with the pointer being
nullified. If an ioctl is already running, the mutex will block the
disconnect path until the ioctl finishes. If an ioctl is blocked waiting
for the lock, it will acquire it after the disconnect routine releases it,
but will then check video_is_registered() (which was cleared by
vb2_video_unregister_device()) and safely return -ENODEV.

Acquiring v4l2_lock after vb2_video_unregister_device() avoids
reintroducing a historical deadlock issue, and usbtv_audio_free() remains
safe as it is called before usbtv_video_free().

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: ksmbd: Denial of service via race condition during concurrent directory operations
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: serialize directory emptiness checks with readdir

SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY holds fp->readdir_lock while it calls iterate_dir()
on fp->filp. An SMB2 SET_INFO request with FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION
can resolve the same FileId and call ksmbd_vfs_empty_dir() on the same
filp without that lock.

iterate_dir()'s inode read lock permits concurrent readers and does not
serialize per-file iterator state. ext4 stores its dx readdir cursor and
fname RB tree in file->private_data. Concurrent reset or refill can
therefore free a fname node while the other worker still traverses it or
retains its RB-tree link, resulting in use-after-free accesses.

An authenticated SMB client with list and delete rights on a directory in
a writable KSMBD share backed by ext4 can trigger this when the directory
takes the dx readdir path. The client overlaps an SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY
request with an SMB2 SET_INFO request carrying FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION
on one live FileId.

In one x86_64 SMP KASAN multi-shot guest using ksmbd-for-next at
171df27077fb, the unmodified kernel reported a cross-worker use-after-free
before a panic. The first report's access and free stacks show the two
request paths directly (trimmed):

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in ext4_htree_store_dirent+0x488/0x550
  Read of size 8 by task kworker/2:0/29
  Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work
  Call Trace:
   ext4_htree_store_dirent+0x488/0x550
   htree_dirblock_to_tree+0x535/0x990
   ext4_htree_fill_tree+0x319/0xba0
   ext4_readdir+0x175a/0x2f40
   iterate_dir+0x1b6/0x630
   smb2_query_dir+0x1003/0x1cc0

  Freed by task 279:
   free_rb_tree_fname+0x67/0xc0
   ext4_readdir+0x13a9/0x2f40
   iterate_dir+0x1b6/0x630
   ksmbd_vfs_empty_dir+0xa2/0x100
   smb2_set_info+0x2ffa/0x45d0

Take fp->readdir_lock across the entire emptiness check. This places both
iterators over that handle's filp in the same lock domain while
preserving the disposition status handling. The exact code change
completed a warning-free x86_64 KASAN bzImage build. Tracing three request
pairs showed that the two iterate_dir() calls no longer overlapped and the
expected statuses were preserved. A further 1,600 reproducer iterations
completed with expected statuses and no KASAN report, Oops, or panic.

The reproducer and complete guest configuration are available privately
to maintainers on request.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: ceph: Denial of Service via null pointer dereference in ceph_readdir
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: fail readdir when the MDS reply carries no dirfrag

A ceph mount oopses in ceph_readdir() when the MDS answers a READDIR
request with a reply whose extra blob is empty.  parse_reply_info()
skips reply blobs whose length is zero, so parse_reply_info_readdir()
never runs, r_reply_info.dir_dir stays NULL, and the reply still
parses as successful.  ceph_mdsc_do_request() returns 0 and
ceph_readdir() then reads rinfo->dir_dir->frag with no NULL check:

	/* extra */
	ceph_decode_32_safe(&p, end, len, bad);
	if (len > 0) {
		...
		err = parse_reply_info_extra(&p, p + len, req, features, s);
		...
	}

The oops on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820, one getdents64(2) on the
mount root after an ms_mode=legacy mount, trimmed:

BUG: KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000000-0x0000000000000007]
Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000000: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 266 Comm: ls Tainted: G                 N  7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
RIP: 0010:ceph_readdir+0xbff/0x3ea0
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 ? __pfx_ceph_readdir+0x10/0x10
 wrap_directory_iterator+0xa2/0xe0
 iterate_dir+0x1da/0x5d0
 __x64_sys_getdents64+0x13b/0x2a0
 do_syscall_64+0xdd/0x4a0
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
 </TASK>

The unconditional frag read came in with 81c6aea5275ea ("ceph: handle
frag mismatch between readdir request and reply"), so the bug is old.

Treat a reply with no dirfrag as a protocol violation: warn once,
drop the request and return -EIO, the same way ceph_readdir() already
handles the two malformed-reply cases later in the function.

Tested on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 (KASAN).  Unpatched, the
getdents64(2) above takes the machine down (oops=panic) on the first
READDIR reply.  With the patch it warns once and getdents64(2)
returns -EIO, no oops, no hang.  A conformant reply for an empty
directory — dirfrag present, zero entries, FRAG_END|FRAG_COMPLETE —
still lists "." and ".." and returns EOF on both kernels, so normal
readdir behavior is unchanged.  The oops is still present in
v7.3-rc5 (72d3fcf802c45).

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via uninitialized key eviction in blk-crypto
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

blk-crypto: fix NULL deref and UAF in __blk_crypto_evict_key()

Sashiko reported a possible NULL pointer dereference, triggered by the
following flow:

  dm-inlinecrypt ctor            # first use of the fallback
   ├─ blk_crypto_init_key()      # succeeds, ctx->key.size != 0
   ├─ blk_crypto_start_using_key()
   │   ├─ hw-wrapped key: -EOPNOTSUPP
   │   │    # profile never allocated (NULL)
   │   └─ raw key: fallback_start_using_mode()
   │      └─ blk_crypto_fallback_init() fails
   │         └─ kfree(profile)   # not NULLed
   ├─ goto bad
   └─ inlinecrypt_dtr()          # evicts whenever key.size is set
      └─ blk_crypto_evict_key()
         └─ blk_crypto_config_supported_natively() = false
            └─ blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key()
               └─ __blk_crypto_evict_key(blk_crypto_fallback_profile)
                  └─ profile->num_slots # BOOM!!!

This issue can be reproduced using the following commands:

  dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/backing bs=1M count=64
  LOOP=$(losetup -f --show /tmp/backing)
  SZ=$(blockdev --getsz $LOOP)
  KEY=$(head -c 64 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
  dmsetup create ic --table "0 $SZ inlinecrypt aes-xts-plain64 \
    $KEY 0 $LOOP 0 1 keytype:hw-wrapped"

And the following oops is triggered:

  ==================================================================
  blk-crypto: loop0: no support for wrapped keys
  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
        0xdffffc000000000b: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000058-0x000000000000005f]
  CPU: 5 UID: 0 PID: 901 Comm: dmsetup 7.3.0-rc3 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
  RIP: 0010:__blk_crypto_evict_key+0x2e/0x3b0
  Call Trace:
   blk_crypto_evict_key+0x24c/0x320
   inlinecrypt_dtr+0xf6/0x160
   inlinecrypt_ctr+0x2d3/0xbd0
   dm_table_add_target+0x661/0xf40
   table_load+0x1c4/0x490
   ctl_ioctl+0x32f/0x5f0
   dm_ctl_ioctl+0xe/0x20
  ==================================================================

dm-inlinecrypt is the only caller that can evict a key that was never
started, as fscrypt frees such a key without evicting it.

Fix this by returning early from blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key() when
tfms_inited[] is not set for the key's mode.  tfms_inited[] is only set
after blk_crypto_fallback_init() has successfully initialized the
profile, so the crash above is no longer reachable.

The bug has been latent since commit c984ff1423ae ("blk-crypto:
dynamically allocate fallback profile") was merged in v6.5, and only
became actually triggerable when commit e7f57d2c47e2 ("dm-inlinecrypt:
add target for inline block device encryption") was merged in v7.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via race condition during core dump handling
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fork: don't create io threads once PF_POSTCOREDUMP is set

zap_process() skips every thread that already has PF_POSTCOREDUMP set.
Such a thread is past synchronize_group_exit(), so a coredump can't
catch it anymore. It isn't counted in core_state->threads_remaining and
it isn't sent SIGKILL.

do_exit() sets PF_POSTCOREDUMP in synchronize_group_exit() and calls
io_uring_files_cancel() right after that. The cancellation runs task
work and a create_worker_cb() that io-wq queued before the exit creates
a new io-wq worker from there. If another thread started a coredump in
the meantime that worker joins a thread-group which is already being
dumped. zap_process() never saw it so it was never counted. But when it
exits it sees signal->core_state in synchronize_group_exit() and
decrements threads_remaining like any other thread.

So the count reaches zero one thread early and the dumper leaves
coredump_wait_inactive() while a thread it counted is still running.

The task has no fatal signal pending because zap_process() deliberately
didn't send it one, and it never went through get_signal() so it doesn't
have PF_SIGNALED either.

Refuse to create an io thread when the creator has PF_POSTCOREDUMP.
That costs nothing. io_uring_files_cancel() raises IO_WQ_BIT_EXIT
before it runs any task work, so a worker created from there only ever
gets to exit again, and io_should_retry_thread() doesn't retry -EINTR.

Clearing PF_POSTCOREDUMP for the new thread in copy_process() was the
other option. It makes the worker a thread like any other, but it only
helps while the dump hasn't started. A worker born after zap_process()
has run is invisible to it whatever its flags say and still decrements
threads_remaining on the way out. Refusing to create it covers both, and
then no task is ever born with the flag, so there is nothing to clear.

Moving io_uring_files_cancel() ahead of synchronize_group_exit() closes
the same window. It runs the cancellation, and whatever that can block
on, before the thread announces itself to the dumper. A thread that
blocks there never reaches coredump_task_exit() at all, so the dumper
ends up waiting for a thread that never parks. Refusing the creation
leaves the cancellation where it is. But it's very ugly to run io_uring
work even before we did all the generic exit work.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via stalled io_uring SQPOLL ring teardown
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/sqpoll: don't wait for the thread to exit

io_sq_thread_stop() wakes the SQPOLL thread and waits for it to exit.
The thread belongs to the thread group that created the ring, so a
SIGSTOP or the cgroup freezer holds it in get_signal(), and the wake up
doesn't change that. io_ring_exit_work() then sleeps in that wait until
someone continues or kills the process. iou_exit has 64 slots, so 64
closed SQPOLL rings of a stopped process keep every other ring from
being freed, for everyone.

Don't wait. Set the stop bit, wake the thread, and let it exit when it
gets to run again. The sqd can now outlive its last ring, so give it a
second refcount with one reference for the rings and one for the thread,
and free it with the last one. The thread can't reach a freed ring,
rings leave ctx_list before dropping their reference, and the io-wq hash
is refcounted.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free in io_uring worker cancellation
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference

io_wq_cancel_tw_create() inspects cb->func after calling
io_worker_cancel_cb(). For an existing worker, that call can drop the
last worker reference and wake io_worker_exit(). If the canceling task
is preempted, the worker can be unlinked and freed by kfree_rcu() before
the callback function is inspected. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free
read in this path.

Save whether the callback belongs to an unpublished continuation worker
while its reference is still held, then use the saved result for the
conditional free. This preserves the existing accounting and frees only
the worker allocated for the canceled continuation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: drm/amdkfd: Avoid integer underflow with ffs in EOP ring size calc
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdkfd: Avoid integer underflow with ffs in EOP ring size calc

The low 6 bits of cp_hqd_eop_control store the base-2 logarithm
of the EOP ring size. This was calculated as

ffs(q->eop_ring_buffer_size / sizeof(unsigned int)) - 1 - 1

But ffs can in theory return 1 or 0, so this could underflow
(although in practice the ring buffer size cannot be less than 4096).

Change this to

ffs(q->eop_ring_buffer_size / sizeof(unsigned int) / 4)

using properties of logarithms.

(cherry picked from commit 4f18c56630383c14bfc6b2d65f88f2f895d2121a)

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: drm/amdkfd: Avoid integer underflow in EOP ring size calculation
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdkfd: Avoid integer underflow in EOP ring size calculation.

The low 6 bits of cp_hqd_eop_control store the base-2 logarithm
of the EOP ring size. This was calculated as

order_base_2(q->eop_ring_buffer_size / 4) - 1

But order_base_2 can in theory return 0, so this could underflow
(although in practice the ring buffer size cannot be less than 4096).

Change this to

order_base_2(q->eop_ring_buffer_size / 8)

using properties of logarithms.

Also add to the above comment to make the mathematics more clear.

(cherry picked from commit f0f43fcf8b2b3a924cad9444340921c96ed5f634)

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: smb: client: drain and invalidate before server-side copy/clone
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: drain and invalidate before server-side copy/clone

cifs_file_copychunk_range() and the clone (FICLONE) path of
cifs_remap_file_range() do not serialise the destination page cache
against the server-side copy the way the other server-side range
operations (smb3_zero_range(), smb3_punch_hole(), smb3_collapse_range()
and smb3_insert_range()) do.

cifs_file_copychunk_range() invalidates the destination range with
filemap_invalidate_inode(), which takes and drops the mapping's
invalidate_lock internally, so the lock is no longer held when the
copychunk ioctl is issued.  It also never drains in-flight netfs I/O on
the target.  The clone path never takes the invalidate_lock at all (only
i_rwsem), uses a bare truncate_inode_pages_range() and likewise does not
drain outstanding I/O.

As a result an asynchronous destination writeback can complete after the
server-side copy/clone has run and reinstate stale data over the region
just written by the server, corrupting the file.  This is the same class
of corruption as commit d7d2adcd022b ("smb/client: flush dirty data
before punching a hole") and has been seen randomly in generic/363
against Windows Server.

Fix both paths to follow the established ordering: hold the target
mapping's invalidate_lock across the flush and invalidation of the
destination and the server ioctl, and call netfs_wait_for_outstanding_io()
on the target to drain in-flight writes before the ioctl is issued.  Only
the target inode's invalidate_lock is required, as the source is merely
flushed and not invalidated; i_rwsem (already held via
lock_two_nondirectories()) is acquired before the invalidate_lock,
matching the VFS lock ordering.  Since filemap_invalidate_inode() takes
that same lock internally, replace it with its own unmap/flush/invalidate
steps instead of calling it, and return early on a zero-length copy to
avoid a range underflow.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: smb: client: flush dirty data before zeroing a range
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: flush dirty data before zeroing a range

smb3_zero_range() emulates FALLOC_FL_ZERO_RANGE by invalidating the
page cache over the target range with truncate_pagecache_range() and
then issuing FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA to the server.

Dirty data was only flushed conditionally, when the range reached or
extended EOF.  For a purely interior zero range that does not reach
EOF, no flush happened, so a dirty folio overlapping the range could
be written back to the server after the FSCTL and refill the range
that was just zeroed with stale data.

Fix this by unconditionally flushing and waiting for dirty data in the
range before invalidating the page cache and issuing
FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA, exactly as was done for smb3_punch_hole() in
commit d7d2adcd022b ("smb/client: flush dirty data before punching a
hole"); the two paths are structurally identical here.

This is observed as generic/363 randomly reading stale data where a
zeroed range is expected against Windows Server.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: smb: client: flush and commit data before querying allocated ranges
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: flush and commit data before querying allocated ranges

The mode 0 / FALLOC_FL_KEEP_SIZE fallocate emulation for small interior
ranges in smb3_simple_fallocate_range() issues
FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES and zero-fills any sub-range the server
reports as an unallocated hole, to force block allocation without
changing file contents.

This is unsafe against Windows servers.  Per the Win32 documentation,
FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES only reports ranges that *may* contain
nonzero data and is explicitly not coherent with recently written data:

  "a call to FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES [after writing to a network
   file] would not necessarily return a correct list of allocated
   regions.  To ensure coherency [...] flush the data to the file"

fsx (generic/363) reproduces the resulting corruption against Windows
Server 2022: a range is written, an uncached read returns the data, yet
the next FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES on that range reports it as a whole
hole, so the emulation overwrites live data with zeroes.  A network trace
confirmed the WRITE, the READ returning data and the query returning an
empty range list within microseconds.  Samba does not exhibit this; its
query is coherent with the written data.

Write back the dirty pages, drain any outstanding I/O and issue an SMB2
FLUSH to force the server to commit the data before querying the
allocated ranges, so the query reflects the data actually present.

With this, generic/363 passes against both Windows Server 2022 and Samba
over 100000 fsx operations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: smb: client: discard post-EOF pagecache when extending a file via clone range
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: discard post-EOF pagecache when extending a file via clone range

cifs_remap_file_range() discarded the pagecache only for the folios
overlapping the destination region, so when a clone extends the file the
folio straddling the old EOF - which may hold data dirtied past EOF
through an mmap - was never dropped and became visible as file content
once the file was extended.

Start the discard at the smaller of fstart and the old EOF.  i_size is
still old here, so nothing past the old EOF is flushed to the server.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: fs: don't silently unmount busy mounts
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fs: don't silently unmount busy mounts

The propagate_mount_busy() helper exists to decide whether a synchronous
can suceed. It does that by looking at the copies of the victims in the
mounts its parent propagates to. One of those functions from propagation
hell.

It skips a copy that has child mounts except for the case of a single
child mount covering the copy's root. That algorithm used to be exact.
It isn't anymore.

Originally only childless copies were unmounted during propagation.
And 1064f874abc0 ("mnt: Tuck mounts under others instead of creating
shadow/side mounts.") ended up adding covered mounts to both sides in
one go.

Along came 99b19d16471e ("mnt: In propgate_umount handle visiting mounts
in any order") and that started to unmount more than before:

[1]: A copy of a mount is unmounted when each of its children is either
     its overmount or a copy of the victim itself. In the former case
     the overmount gets reparented. In the latter case the copy of the
     victim will end up being unmounted.

So propagate_umount() ended up being rewritten without adjusting
propagate_mount_busy(). And currently propagate_mount_busy() doesn't
look at copies of the victim that have two or more children nor a single
child that is not the overmount.

So any such copy in [1] is not checked for
references. The result is that a synchronous unmount succeeds, pulling
out a mount that is still in use.

A container can run into this with its own mounts. The host shares a
tree with the container and the host has a mount in that tree:

  mount -t tmpfs none /mnt
  mount --make-shared /mnt
  mount -t tmpfs none /mnt/a

The container's /mnt is a slave copy of the host mount. The container
now takes a detached copy of the tree and mounts that copy beneath its
propagated copy of /mnt/a and keeps the file descriptor to the tree
open:

  unshare -m --propagation unchanged
  mount --make-rslave /
  fd = open_tree(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt", OPEN_TREE_CLONE | AT_RECURSIVE)
  move_mount(fd, "", AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/a", MOVE_MOUNT_BENEATH)

  grep /mnt /proc/self/mountinfo
  775 355 ... /mnt ...     master:646
  777 775 ... /mnt/a ...   master:646
  776 777 ... /mnt/a ...   master:647
  778 777 ... /mnt/a/a ... master:647

The now attached tree (777) is now mounted beneath the container's copy
of /mnt/a. That's also where the host mount sits (as seen from the host
mount namespace). So the propagated copy (776) of the host's mount is on
top of its root and the copy of that (778) is inside it. Now the host
runs:

  umount /mnt/a

and it succeeds. The moved tree tree and the copy inside of it are gone
from the container. Now only the propagated copy is left and it got
reparented to where it was before:

  grep /mnt /proc/self/mountinfo
  775 355 ... /mnt ... master:646
  776 775 ... /mnt/a ...

But the file descriptor still refers to the moved tree. So a synchronous
umount detached a mount that is still in use.

Teach propagate_mount_busy() the same checks that propagate_umount()
does. It now checks for a single victim mount without children
for which it can assume that MNT_LOCKED is cleared on every copy like
propagate_umount() does. The copies form chains. IOW, when a copy itself
receives propagation from the victim's parent then the mount at the same
mountpoint inside that copy is a copy as well. Whether a mount receives
propagation from the victim's can simply be checked by walking its
masters. Walk each chain once from its top so we are sure that nested
copies stay linear. Check every reference once of every copy that gets
unmounted.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: net: team: free skb when broadcast has no txable port
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: team: free skb when broadcast has no txable port

bc_transmit() sends the original skb through the last txable port.
When no port is txable, it returns false without consuming the skb, but
team_xmit() still returns NETDEV_TX_OK. AF_PACKET sends then retain the
skb and its socket write-memory charge.

A TX-enabled, link-down port keeps the broadcast transmit op installed.
Carrier can stay up through a second link-up, TX-disabled port or be
forced on by userspace. Free the original skb on the no-port path while
leaving the existing drop accounting intact.

Discovered by Sashiko during review of previous commit.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: ipc: drop the mqueue mount with kern_unmount() on setup failure
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipc: drop the mqueue mount with kern_unmount() on setup failure

mq_init_ns() creates the mqueue mount with fc_mount_longterm(), so its
->mnt_ns is MNT_NS_INTERNAL. When setting up the mqueue or ipc sysctls
or msg_init_ns() fails afterwards, create_ipc_ns() drops it with a plain
mntput(). With ->mnt_ns set that takes the fast path of
mntput_no_expire(). The count drops to zero and nothing ever kills the
mount, so the mount and the mqueue superblock are leaked.

Commit dc55e35f9e81 ("ipc: Store mqueue sysctls in the ipc namespace")
added the first failure path after mq_init_ns() and never dropped the
mount. Commit 7229d74e5e8c ("ipc: create_ipc_ns: drop mqueue mount on
sysctl setup failure") tried to fix that with a mntput() but that
doesn't help for a long-term mount.

Use kern_unmount(). free_ipc() open-codes the same thing for a namespace
that made it.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: information disclosure via uninitialized stack memory in KVM SynIC message delivery
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Zero reserved synic flags when delivering message to avoid stack leak

Ensure all reserved flags are zeroed when setting the msg_pending flag as
part of SynIC message delivery, as setting only msg_pending can leak seven
bits of kernel stack data to the guest.  E.g. gcc typically uses a
bitwise-OR to set the msg_pending flag, without initializing the on-stack
variable.

Precisely zero the flags, e.g. as opposed to zeroing the entire structure,
to make it somewhat more obvious that the flags *need* to be zeroed.  E.g.
it would be quite easy to misread the initial read of guest memory and
think that zeroing the entire structure is completely superfluous.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via improper caching of empty group replies in SUNRPC
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sunrpc: treat empty auth.unix.gid replies as negative entries

When rpc.mountd cannot resolve a uid (getpwuid() or getgrouplist()
failure, e.g. while winbind or sssd is briefly unreachable), it
answers the auth.unix.gid upcall with zero groups. unix_gid_parse()
installs that as a valid positive entry, and svcauth_unix_set_client()
then replaces the credential's group list with the empty one on
every request, RPCSEC_GSS included via svcauth_gss_set_client().
One failed lookup strips that uid of all supplementary groups on
every export for up to mountd's configured TTL (30 minutes by
default), long after the NSS backend has recovered.

mountd cannot send an empty list for a successful lookup, since
getgrouplist(3) always includes at least the user's primary group,
so a zero-group reply can only mean the lookup failed. Record it as
a negative entry: unix_gid_find() then returns -ENOENT and
svcauth_unix_set_client() keeps the groups the RPC credential
already carries. This is the fallback that
commit 3fc605a2aa38 ("[PATCH] knfsd: allow the server to provide a
gid list when using AUTH_UNIX authentication") promised when no
answer is available, and the same state try_to_negate_entry()
already creates when no listener holds the channel open.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via unvalidated transport name in NFSD listener configuration
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: validate transport name in listener_set before serv creation

nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() holds nfsd_mutex for the whole listener
teardown and rebuild. The code checks NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME for
presence only, and not for content. An arbitrary name therefore reaches
svc_xprt_create_from_sa(). There, a name that matches no registered class
calls request_module("svc%s", name). That call is a TASK_KILLABLE usermode
helper upcall, and it runs under nfsd_mutex.

Check the name against the classes that NFSD can create: tcp, udp and
rdma. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), which runs before
the code takes nfsd_mutex. The rejection names the offending attribute
through extack, since -EPROTONOSUPPORT on its own does not say which
entry carried the bad name.

This narrows the upcall. It does not remove it. NFSD accepts "rdma"
without a condition, so on a kernel that does not build svcrdma the name
still reaches request_module("svcrdma") under nfsd_mutex. That is
necessary for the modular case, where the autoload is legitimate.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: nfsd: Denial of Service via cache entry leak in idtoname_parse()
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: Fix id-to-name cache entry leak in idtoname_parse()

idtoname_lookup() returns the id-to-name cache entry with a new
reference. The name is parsed between the lookup and the update call,
and when the parsed name is malformed (negative length or longer than
IDMAP_NAMESZ), idtoname_parse() jumps to the error label without
dropping the reference returned by idtoname_lookup(), leaking the cache
entry.

Release the reference with cache_put() before taking the error exit.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Data corruption via missing lock validation in NFS flexfiles client
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSv4/flexfiles: fail I/O to the data server once a lock is lost

When a client loses a byte-range lock, because its lease expired and it
may not recover the lock (nfs.recover_lost_locks=0) or because reclaim
failed, it marks the lock state NFS_LOCK_LOST and fails further I/O by
that lock owner.  Otherwise an application that believes it holds a
lock over a range is never told that the lock is gone, and can
overwrite data that another client has since written under its own
lock on that range.

The NFSv4 READ/WRITE and file layout I/O paths apply this in
rpc_call_prepare, where nfs4_set_rw_stateid() returns -EIO for a lost
lock.  The flexfiles data server I/O path does not: the NFSv3 data
server path never checked, and the check on the NFSv4 path was removed
when the data server stateid began to be taken from the layout.

Fail read and write RPCs to the data server in rpc_call_prepare when the
lock is lost.  The data server path has no use for the stateid that
nfs4_set_rw_stateid() selects, and selecting it looks up a delegation
or open stateid on every I/O.
Instead add nfs4_lock_context_lost(), which only tests NFS_LOCK_LOST,
and check it alongside the open state.  Its lookup,
__nfs4_lookup_lock_state(), is split out of __nfs4_find_lock_state()
and takes no reference: a lock state is only unlinked from
state->lock_states under state->state_lock, so one found while holding
that lock cannot be freed before it is released.  Use it in
nfs4_copy_lock_stateid() as well, which only reads the lock state under
that lock.  That drops a reference get and put from stateid selection
for all NFSv4 I/O without changing the stateid selected.

Terminating the RPC in rpc_call_prepare is not enough on its own.  The
done callback reads the -EIO as a data server connection error, forgets
the device ID, and resets the I/O to pNFS (or, for an NFSv4 data
server, possibly to the MDS).  After a reset to pNFS a new LAYOUTGET is
granted and rpc_call_prepare fails the I/O again, without end.  The
existing NFS_CONTEXT_BAD check does not loop, since the open state is
then invalid and pnfs_update_layout() fails the reset I/O, but it still
forgets the device ID.

So when an RPC that was never sent fails and the open context is bad,
the open state is invalid, or the lock is lost, complete it with -EIO
without error handling.  An RPC that was sent and failed is handled as
before, so a real data server error is still reported to the MDS.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: File system metadata corruption via incorrect block accounting in XFS repair
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: don't subtract excess usage twice when computing agf_btreeblks

LOLLM noticed that the free space btree repair code calculates
agf_btreeblks from the number of blocks we wrote to rebuild the free
space btrees (minus the roots).  That's correct.  However, it observes
that we subtract the "excess" reservation, which is not correct.  Fix
this accounting problem.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: improper access control via stale cached ACLs during XFS repair
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: always forget cached ACLs if the attr fork swap succeeds

LOLLM complains that xrep_xattr_rebuild_tree omits the xfs_forget_acl
call if the attr fork swap succeeds (and hence the acls might have
changed) but reaping the old attr fork fails.  Fix it so that we always
purge the cached acls if the swap succeeds, even if subsequent steps do
not.  This avoids some cache coherency problems with access controls.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service in OverlayFS via empty security capabilities
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: skip copy up of empty security.capability

ovl_copy_xattr() gives up if it can't read an attribute that
listxattr() has named.  An empty security.capability, which anybody has
been able to store on any file for a long time, is such a case: it is
listed, and getxattr() has nothing to return for it.  A file in a lower
layer that carries one can't be copied up: it can't be written to,
renamed or have its mode changed.

There is nothing to copy if there are no data.  Go on with the next
one.

[amir: treat -EINVAL as no capability too, and do the same in
 ovl_copy_up_meta_inode_data()]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service in OverlayFS via race condition during file creation
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: set the revalidate flags after d_instantiate()

stat() of a file on an overlayfs mount triggers a kernel warning and
fails with ECHILD if another task is creating that file at the same
time. This happens on an overlay with a FUSE upper layer, which is the
layer where overlayfs creates new files. Write access to a directory on
such an overlay is all a user needs to run the two tasks.

The revalidate flags are DCACHE_OP_REVALIDATE and
DCACHE_OP_WEAK_REVALIDATE. They tell path walk to call ->d_revalidate()
or ->d_weak_revalidate() on a dentry, so that the filesystem can check
that the cached dentry is still valid. An overlay dentry only has one of
these flags if a dentry in one of its layers has it. FUSE dentries have
the first one.

When a flag is set on an overlay dentry, path walk calls
ovl_dentry_revalidate_common(). That function only expects a dentry
without an inode in RCU walk, while the dentry is being destroyed. For
such a dentry outside of RCU walk, it hits a WARN_ON() and
returns -ECHILD. So a negative overlay dentry must never have the flags
set.

ovl_instantiate() breaks this rule. When a task creates a file, the
overlay dentry for the new name is hashed but still negative.
ovl_instantiate() then works in this order:

- It copies the flags from the new upper dentry to the overlay dentry.
- It calls ovl_get_inode(), which can sleep in a getxattr request to the
  FUSE server.
- Only then does it call d_instantiate().

A second task that looks up the name between the first step and the last
finds a negative dentry with the flags set and revalidates it.

Reproduced with a FUSE server that delays its getxattr reply: stat() of
a name that was being created hit the WARN_ON() and failed with ECHILD.

Fix this by setting the flags after d_instantiate().

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: information disclosure via uninitialized extended attribute copy-up in OverlayFS
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: do not copy up an xattr value that was never read

Copy-up stores uninitialized kernel memory in an xattr of the upper
file, where the user can read it.

ovl_copy_xattr() may only pass bytes to ovl_do_setxattr() that
ovl_do_getxattr() has read. When the read fails with -ERANGE the
function asks for the size again, and if the new size fits the buffer
it stores the buffer although nothing was read into it. The buffer
comes from kvmalloc(), or it still holds the value of the previous
xattr.

A FUSE lower layer that answers every sized GETXATTR with -ERANGE made
copy-up store 4096 bytes that the server never sent, with a kernel
pointer in them, as an xattr of the upper file.

Fix this by failing the copy-up with -EIO when the size that follows
-ERANGE fits the buffer.

Vulnerabilities.Title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:  x ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: always report inode repair setup failures

LOLLM noticed that xchk_setup_inode silently discards errors being
returned by xrep_setup_inode.  Fix that, and fix the stub macro so that
it actually "returns" a value.

Vulnerabilities.Title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:  x ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: check fork type against dabtree block magic number

LOLLM complains that we fail to flag dabtree blocks that should never be
associated with the file fork -- data forks can't point to xattr leaves,
and attr forks can't point to dirent blocks.  Add the missing checks.

Vulnerabilities.Title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:  x ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: don't proceed with xattr repair if the live update fails

LOLLM observes that we ought to make one last check for failed live
updates before replacing the xattr structure.  Let's be cautious here.

Vulnerabilities.Title: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:  s ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/probes: Fix wrong opcode for cgrb fixup

The last byte of the cgrb instruction is 0xe4, however the probes code
compares against 0xe6. Fix it.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB server: SQL injection vulnerability via improper handling of big5 character set with mysql_real_escape_string()
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. In versions 3.3.18 and 3.4.8, an application that was taking non-validated user input, escaping it with mysql_real_escape_string() and sending it to the database using text protocol and big5 character set was vulnerable to SQL injections, even though mysql_real_escape_string() was supposed to prevent them. This issue has been patched in versions 3.3.19 and 3.4.9.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB Server: Arbitrary code execution via wsrep_notify_cmd
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. Versions 10.6.1 through 10.6.26, 10.11.1 through 10.11.17, 11.4.1 through 11.4.11, 11.8.1 through 11.8.7, and 12.3.1 with  `wsrep_notify_cmd` enabled would execute shell commands embedded in the name of the joiner node. This is fixed in 10.6.27, 10.11.18, 11.4.12, 11.8.8, and 12.3.2. As a workaround, anyone who cannot upgrade now should disable `wsrep_notify_cmd`.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB: Unauthorized table access via unencoded partition names
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.11.1 until 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, ALTER TABLE ... CONVERT ... PARTITION does not apply filename encoding to user-specified partition names before using them in filesystem path construction. An authenticated database user can use a partition name requiring filename escaping to make the conversion operate on table files the user is not authorized to access, allowing unauthorized table reads or modifications. This issue is fixed in versions 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Arbitrary code execution via CONNECT engine out-of-bounds write
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the CONNECT engine's DOS table type used an incorrect boundary check that permitted a one-byte null write beyond a stack buffer at an attacker-controlled offset. An authenticated user able to use the CONNECT engine could cause a crash and potentially remote code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Privilege escalation via environment variable injection during service restart
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the mariadb.service unit used /run/mysqld/wsrep-new-cluster during the next service restart. A database user with FILE privilege and a secure-file-priv configuration permitting writes to /run/mysqld could create that file and inject attacker-controlled environment values into the restarted service. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Privilege escalation via unescaped newlines in view parser
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the MariaDB view FRM parser did not safely encode embedded newline characters in a username. An account with CREATE USER and CREATE VIEW WITH GRANT OPTION could create a crafted username containing additional view metadata, causing the parser to interpret part of the username as security metadata and potentially escalating database privileges. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: Arbitrary Code Execution via improper parameter validation during State Snapshot Transfer
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 10.6.1 to before 10.6.26, 10.11.1 to before 10.11.17, 11.4.1 to before 11.4.11, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.7, and 12.3.1, during the SST the donor node is interpolating parameters that the joiner sent into the command line. Not all parameters were properly validated which could allow a malicious joiner to execute arbitrary shell commands on the donor side via the mariabackup SST method. This issue has been patched in versions 10.6.26, 10.11.17, 11.4.11, 11.8.7, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mbstream: Unauthorized file creation via path traversal
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 10.6.1 to before 10.6.26, 10.11.1 to before 10.11.17, 11.4.1 to before 11.4.11, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.7, and 12.3.1, mbstream did not check for /../ in the path when unpacking the archive. A proper backup can never contain such paths, but a specially crafted archive could have caused mbstream to create files outside of the target-dir path. This issue has been patched in versions 10.6.26, 10.11.17, 11.4.11, 11.8.7, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: Arbitrary code execution via improper parameter validation during SST
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 10.6.1 to before 10.6.27, 10.11.1 to before 10.11.18, 11.4.1 to before 11.4.12, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.8, and 12.3.1, during the SST the donor node is interpolating parameters that the joiner sent into the command line. Not all parameters were properly validated which could allow a malicious joiner to execute arbitrary shell commands on the donor side via the rsync SST method. This issue has been patched in versions 10.6.27, 10.11.18, 11.4.12, 11.8.8, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: Arbitrary code execution via global system variable manipulation by a high-privileged user
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 10.6.1 to before 10.6.27, 10.11.1 to before 10.11.18, 11.4.1 to before 11.4.12, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.8, and 12.3.1, a high-privileged MariaDB user could've used wsrep_sst_receive_address or wsrep_sst_donor global system variables to execute shell commands as the uid of the mariadbd process on the galera joiner node. This issue has been patched in versions 10.6.27, 10.11.18, 11.4.12, 11.8.8, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB: Out-of-bound buffer write on in `ST_AsText` of nested GeometryCollections
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, ST_AsText can write beyond an allocated output buffer when converting deeply nested GeometryCollections because recursive WKT serialization does not account for bytes consumed or reserve sufficient space. A low-privileged remote attacker can submit a specially crafted GIS object to corrupt memory and potentially achieve code execution when combined with another vulnerability. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: SQL injection via improper identifier quoting
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, SHOW CREATE SERVER, SHOW CREATE USER, and mariadb-dump are affected because each does not consistently quote identifiers and values when serializing SQL. A low-privileged attacker can trigger the issue when an attacker-created object with crafted identifiers or values is included in SHOW output or a dump, then create an object with crafted identifiers or values so generated SQL contains injected statements and execute attacker-injected SQL when the poisoned output is applied. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB: Numerous issues caused by historical #mysql50# tablename encoding bypass.
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the #mysql50# bypass prefix is affected because it allows the #mysql50# prefix to bypass normal table-name filesystem encoding. An attacker can trigger the issue with a table name using the #mysql50# prefix, then use a #mysql50# table name to access files under their legacy unencoded name and cause crashes, data corruption, data exfiltration, or remote code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Privilege escalation via empty password in GRANT PROXY statement
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the GRANT PROXY statement treats an IDENTIFIED clause with an empty password as though authentication were not specified, causing it to check the wrong grantor privileges. A low-privileged attacker who can name another account can exploit this authorization error to set that account's password. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Information disclosure via embedded null bytes in query cache plugin
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the qc_info plugin could be confused by a query containing embedded null bytes. Reading information_schema.query_cache_info after such a query was cached could access data beyond the end of a heap-allocated buffer, potentially disclosing adjacent memory or crashing the server. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Denial of Service via invalid binary JSON in mysql_json plugin
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the mysql_json plugin assumed that imported MySQL tables contained valid MySQL binary JSON data. A specially prepared MySQL table containing invalid JSON data could cause out-of-bounds reads, information disclosure, or a server crash. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: Arbitrary code execution via crafted FRM metadata
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, MariaDB insufficiently validated counts, offsets, lengths, and field boundaries in FRM metadata while opening binary FRM files. An attacker able to place a crafted FRM file in the data directory could trigger out-of-bounds reads or writes, crash the server, or potentially execute code. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB: Privilege escalation via ACL cache key collision
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, MariaDB's ACL cache could generate the same database-privilege cache key for role and localhost user names that matched because both used an empty IP component. An attacker with CREATE USER could create the colliding principal and, when the original principal's database privileges were cached, exercise privileges assigned to the other account. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB server: Information disclosure of stored routine definitions due to insufficient privilege check
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 11.4.1 to before 11.4.11, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.7, and 12.3.1, a user getting EXECUTE access to a stored routine via a role, could see the routine definition even without SHOW CREATE ROUTINE privilege. This issue has been patched in versions 11.4.11, 11.8.7, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB: Privilege bypass allows unauthorized file write via subqueries
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From versions 10.6.1 to before 10.6.26, 10.11.1 to before 10.11.17, 11.4.1 to before 11.4.11, 11.8.1 to before 11.8.7, and 12.3.1, MariaDB allowed SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE and SELECT ... INTO DUMPFILE without verifying the FILE privilege if the FROM clause contained only subqueries. This issue has been patched in versions 10.6.26, 10.11.17, 11.4.11, 11.8.7, and 12.3.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mysql: mariadb: Replication unspecified vulnerability (CPU Jul 2026)
Vulnerabilities.Description: Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: Server: Replication).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.10, 9.7.0-9.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.47, 8.4.0-8.4.10 and  9.7.0-9.7.1. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.9 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: mariadb: out-of-bounds read in ST_Area with crafted MULTIPOLYGON
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, ST_Area reads beyond the allocated buffer when processing invalid WKB for a MultiPolygon because the multi-polygon parser advances past a nested geometry header without first verifying enough input remains. A low-privileged remote attacker can supply malformed spatial data to disclose memory useful for bypassing ASLR as part of a multi-vulnerability chain. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Vulnerabilities.Title: mariadb: MariaDB: Unauthorized file access via CONNECT engine functions
Vulnerabilities.Description: MariaDB server is a community developed fork of MySQL server. From 10.6.1 until 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2, the CONNECT engine plugin file-access UDFs json_file(), bson_file(), jfile_make(), bfile_make(), and jbin_file() are affected because each does not enforce FILE privilege or the secure_file_priv setting. A low-privileged attacker can trigger the issue by calling a CONNECT file-access UDF with a filesystem path, then invoke a CONNECT file-access UDF to access a filesystem path and read or write files that the database account is not authorized to access, subject to operating-system permissions. This issue is fixed in versions 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, and 13.0.2.

Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized read access to a subset of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 2.7 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N).

Vulnerabilities.Title: patch: Filename validation bypass in reversal fallback allows file creation outside the working directory
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GNU patch. An attacker can achieve arbitrary file creation outside the intended working directory by enticing a user or automated workflow to apply a specially crafted patch file. Due to missing validation during automatic patch reversal, absolute file paths in patch headers are accepted rather than rejected. Consequently, the utility can create files in arbitrary locations with the permissions of the executing user.

Vulnerabilities.Title: zlib: zlib: Heap buffer overflow in gz_vacate() allows arbitrary code execution
Vulnerabilities.Description: zlib 1.2.11 through 1.3.2 contains a heap buffer overflow: after an underlying write() fails, gz_write() returns without resetting strm.next_in, leaving it pointed at the caller's buffer. A later gz* write call then derives a position from the stale pointer and writes past a heap allocation; any write() failure reaches it, including EPIPE on a blocking descriptor, and in versions before 1.3.1.2 the failed write must be followed by a gzclearerr() call.

Vulnerabilities.Title: zlib: zlib: Denial of Service via infinite loop in CRC32 combine functions
Vulnerabilities.Description: zlib before 1.3.2 allows CPU consumption via crc32_combine64 and crc32_combine_gen64 because x2nmodp can do right shifts within a loop that has no termination condition.

Vulnerabilities.Title: zlib: zlib: Heap buffer overflow in gz_vacate() allows arbitrary code execution
Vulnerabilities.Description: zlib 1.2.11 through 1.3.2 contains a heap buffer overflow: after an underlying write() fails, gz_write() returns without resetting strm.next_in, leaving it pointed at the caller's buffer. A later gz* write call then derives a position from the stale pointer and writes past a heap allocation; any write() failure reaches it, including EPIPE on a blocking descriptor, and in versions before 1.3.1.2 the failed write must be followed by a gzclearerr() call.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pip: pip missing checks on symbolic link extraction
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When extracting a tar archive pip may not check symbolic links point into the extraction directory if the tarfile module doesn't implement PEP 706.
Note that upgrading pip to a "fixed" version for this vulnerability doesn't fix all known vulnerabilities that are remediated by using a Python version that implements PEP 706.

Note that this is a vulnerability in pip's fallback implementation of tar extraction for Python versions that don't implement PEP 706
and therefore are not secure to all vulnerabilities in the Python 'tarfile' module. If you're using a Python version that implements PEP 706
then pip doesn't use the "vulnerable" fallback code.

Mitigations include upgrading to a version of pip that includes the fix, upgrading to a Python version that implements PEP 706 (Python >=3.9.17, >=3.10.12, >=3.11.4, or >=3.12),
applying the linked patch, or inspecting source distributions (sdists) before installation as is already a best-practice.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pip: pip: Arbitrary file installation via malicious package indexes
Vulnerabilities.Description:
pip would incorrectly handle doubly-encoded package URLs from indexes allowing for files to be installed to arbitrary locations on disk even when installing wheels.




This vulnerability requires downloading or installing a package from a malicious package index to succeed, malicious packages alone are not able to exploit this vulnerability. Note that this vulnerability only materially impacts users running `pip download` with the `--only-binary` option as installing source distributions from an untrusted index is already an unsafe operation that executes code during install time.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pip: pip: Incorrect file installation due to improper archive handling
Vulnerabilities.Description: pip handles concatenated tar and ZIP files as ZIP files regardless of filename or whether a file is both a tar and ZIP file. This behavior could result in confusing installation behavior, such as installing "incorrect" files according to the filename of the archive. New behavior only proceeds with installation if the file identifies uniquely as a ZIP or tar archive, not as both.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pip: pip: Arbitrary code execution or information disclosure via malicious wheel package installation
Vulnerabilities.Description: pip prior to version 26.1 would run self-update check functionality after installing wheel files which required importing well-known Python modules names. These module imports were intentionally deferred to increase startup time of the pip CLI. The patch changes self-update functionality to run before wheels are installed to prevent newly-installed modules from being imported shortly after the installation of a wheel package. Users should still review package contents prior to installation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: python-pip: Path traversal via malicious entry point name in pip wheel installation allows arbitrary file overwrite
Vulnerabilities.Description: pip would treat console_scripts and gui_scripts as paths instead of file names without sanitizing the resolved absolute path to the installation directory, leading to entry points being installed outside the installation directory.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pip: pip: Information disclosure via path traversal when installing crafted wheel archives
Vulnerabilities.Description: When pip is installing and extracting a maliciously crafted wheel archive, files may be extracted outside the installation directory. The path traversal is limited to prefixes of the installation directory, thus isn't able to inject or overwrite executable files in typical situations.
